import { NextResponse } from "next/server";
import { decodePolyline, haversineM, type LngLat } from "@/lib/geometry";

const NB_SNAP_URL = "https://api.nextbillion.io/snapToRoads/json";
const MAX_POINTS = 100;

export interface SnappedPoint {
  lng: number;
  lat: number;
  originalIndex: number;
  name?: string;
  distance?: number;
}

export interface SnapCoverage {
  /** Points sent to NB. */
  sent: number;
  /** Points NB reported as matched (after any repair calls). */
  matched: number;
  /** Indices of sent points NB did not match. */
  unmatchedIndices: number[];
  /** True if a leading run of points had to be re-snapped separately. */
  headRepaired: boolean;
  /** True if a trailing run of points had to be re-snapped separately. */
  tailRepaired: boolean;
  /** True if the final geometry still doesn't reach the start and end of the path. */
  partial: boolean;
}

export interface SnapResponse {
  /** Snapped route geometry as [lng, lat] pairs. */
  coordinates: LngLat[];
  /** Each input point projected onto the road network. */
  snappedPoints: SnappedPoint[];
  /** Total snapped-route length in metres, as reported by NB. */
  distance: number | null;
  /** Snap radius (metres) that finally produced a match. */
  radiusUsedM: number;
  /** Number of snapToRoads calls made (radius escalation + coverage repair). */
  attempts: number;
  coverage: SnapCoverage;
  /** ISO country code reported by NB (`detail=true`), when available. */
  countryCode: string | null;
}

// When NB can't match a sparse / rough trace at the requested radius, retry
// with progressively larger radii before giving up.
const RADIUS_ESCALATION = [1, 2.5, 6, 12];
const MAX_RADIUS_M = 1000;
const NO_MATCH_RE = /could not match/i;
// A head/tail run of at least this many unmatched points triggers a repair call.
const MIN_REPAIR_RUN = 2;
// The geometry must end within this distance of the path's end to count as complete.
const COMPLETE_TOLERANCE_M = 400;

interface SnapRequestBody {
  /** [lng, lat] pairs of the hand-drawn path. */
  path: LngLat[];
  /** Snap radius in metres applied to every point (default 25). */
  radiusM?: number;
  mode?: "car" | "truck";
}

interface NbResult {
  coordinates: LngLat[];
  snappedPoints: SnappedPoint[];
  distance: number | null;
  countryCode: string | null;
}

type NbCall =
  | { ok: true; result: NbResult }
  | { ok: false; error: string; status: number; noMatch: boolean };

function extractCoordinates(data: any): LngLat[] {
  // NB returns a GeoJSON Feature wrapping a (Multi)LineString geometry.
  const rawGj = data?.geojson;
  const gj = rawGj?.type === "Feature" ? rawGj.geometry : rawGj;
  if (gj?.type === "LineString" && Array.isArray(gj.coordinates)) {
    return gj.coordinates as LngLat[];
  }
  if (gj?.type === "MultiLineString" && Array.isArray(gj.coordinates)) {
    return (gj.coordinates as LngLat[][]).flat();
  }
  const encoded: string[] = Array.isArray(data?.geometry)
    ? data.geometry
    : typeof data?.geometry === "string"
      ? [data.geometry]
      : [];
  const out: LngLat[] = [];
  for (const g of encoded) {
    const six = decodePolyline(g, 6);
    // Heuristic: polyline5 decoded as 6 collapses to tiny values.
    const plausible =
      six.every(([lng, lat]) => Math.abs(lng) <= 180 && Math.abs(lat) <= 90) &&
      six.some(([lng, lat]) => Math.abs(lng) > 0.5 || Math.abs(lat) > 0.5);
    out.push(...(plausible ? six : decodePolyline(g, 5)));
  }
  return out;
}

async function callSnap(
  apiKey: string,
  path: LngLat[],
  radius: number,
  mode: "car" | "truck",
): Promise<NbCall> {
  const params = new URLSearchParams({
    key: apiKey,
    // NB expects lat,lng pairs separated by |
    path: path.map(([lng, lat]) => `${lat},${lng}`).join("|"),
    geometry: "geojson",
    tolerate_outlier: "true",
    detail: "true",
    mode,
    radiuses: path.map(() => String(radius)).join("|"),
  });
  const r = await fetch(`${NB_SNAP_URL}?${params.toString()}`);
  const text = await r.text();
  let data: any;
  try {
    data = JSON.parse(text);
  } catch {
    return {
      ok: false,
      error: `non-JSON from NB (${r.status}): ${text.slice(0, 200)}`,
      status: 502,
      noMatch: false,
    };
  }
  const ok = r.ok && (!data?.status || String(data.status).toLowerCase() === "ok");
  if (!ok) {
    const error = String(
      data?.msg ?? data?.message ?? data?.error ?? `snapToRoads failed (${r.status})`,
    );
    return { ok: false, error, status: r.ok ? 502 : r.status, noMatch: NO_MATCH_RE.test(error) };
  }
  const rawPoints = data?.snappedPoints ?? data?.snapped_points;
  const snappedPoints: SnappedPoint[] = Array.isArray(rawPoints)
    ? rawPoints.map((sp: any) => ({
        lng: Number(sp?.location?.longitude),
        lat: Number(sp?.location?.latitude),
        originalIndex: Number(sp?.originalIndex ?? sp?.original_index ?? -1),
        name: sp?.name || undefined,
        distance: typeof sp?.distance === "number" ? sp.distance : undefined,
      }))
    : [];
  return {
    ok: true,
    result: {
      coordinates: extractCoordinates(data),
      snappedPoints,
      distance: typeof data?.distance === "number" ? data.distance : null,
      countryCode: typeof data?.country_code === "string" ? data.country_code : null,
    },
  };
}

function pathLength(c: LngLat[]): number {
  let t = 0;
  for (let i = 1; i < c.length; i++) t += haversineM(c[i - 1], c[i]);
  return t;
}

export async function POST(request: Request) {
  const apiKey = process.env.NB_API_KEY;
  if (!apiKey) {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: "NB_API_KEY not configured" }, { status: 500 });
  }
  let body: SnapRequestBody;
  try {
    body = await request.json();
  } catch {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: "invalid JSON body" }, { status: 400 });
  }
  const path = Array.isArray(body.path) ? body.path : [];
  const valid = path.every(
    (p) =>
      Array.isArray(p) &&
      p.length === 2 &&
      Number.isFinite(p[0]) &&
      Number.isFinite(p[1]) &&
      Math.abs(p[0]) <= 180 &&
      Math.abs(p[1]) <= 90,
  );
  if (!valid || path.length < 2) {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: "path must contain at least 2 [lng,lat] points" }, { status: 400 });
  }
  if (path.length > MAX_POINTS) {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: `path may contain at most ${MAX_POINTS} points` }, { status: 400 });
  }
  const mode: "car" | "truck" = body.mode === "truck" ? "truck" : "car";

  const baseRadius =
    Number.isFinite(Number(body.radiusM)) && Number(body.radiusM) > 0 ? Number(body.radiusM) : 25;
  const radii = Array.from(
    new Set(RADIUS_ESCALATION.map((m) => Math.min(MAX_RADIUS_M, Math.round(baseRadius * m)))),
  );

  // ---- primary call, escalating the radius on "could not match" ------------
  let primary: NbResult | null = null;
  let lastError = "snapToRoads failed";
  let lastStatus = 502;
  let radiusUsedM = radii[0];
  let attempts = 0;
  for (const radius of radii) {
    attempts++;
    radiusUsedM = radius;
    const call = await callSnap(apiKey, path, radius, mode);
    if (call.ok) {
      primary = call.result;
      break;
    }
    lastError = call.error;
    lastStatus = call.status;
    if (!call.noMatch) break; // only escalate on "no match"
  }
  if (!primary) {
    return NextResponse.json(
      {
        error: NO_MATCH_RE.test(lastError)
          ? `${lastError} (tried snap radii up to ${radiusUsedM} m). Try drawing closer to roads or a shorter route.`
          : lastError,
        attempts,
      },
      { status: lastStatus === 422 ? 422 : lastStatus },
    );
  }

  // ---- coverage repair -----------------------------------------------------
  // NB silently drops points it can't fit into the match (tolerate_outlier).
  // Interior gaps are fine — the geometry still routes across them — but if a
  // run at the START or END is dropped the returned geometry simply stops
  // short. Re-snap those runs on their own (anchored on the nearest matched
  // point) and stitch the geometry back together.
  let coordinates = primary.coordinates.slice();
  let snappedPoints = primary.snappedPoints.slice();
  let distance = primary.distance;
  const matched = new Set(snappedPoints.map((p) => p.originalIndex));
  let headRepaired = false;
  let tailRepaired = false;

  const matchedIdx = [...matched].filter((i) => i >= 0 && i < path.length).sort((a, b) => a - b);
  if (matchedIdx.length) {
    const firstMatched = matchedIdx[0];
    const lastMatched = matchedIdx[matchedIdx.length - 1];

    if (lastMatched < path.length - 1 && path.length - 1 - lastMatched >= MIN_REPAIR_RUN) {
      const sub = path.slice(lastMatched);
      const call = await callSnap(apiKey, sub, Math.min(MAX_RADIUS_M, radiusUsedM * 2.5), mode);
      attempts++;
      if (call.ok && call.result.coordinates.length >= 2) {
        coordinates = coordinates.concat(call.result.coordinates);
        snappedPoints = snappedPoints.concat(
          call.result.snappedPoints
            .filter((p) => p.originalIndex > 0)
            .map((p) => ({ ...p, originalIndex: p.originalIndex + lastMatched })),
        );
        distance = distance != null && call.result.distance != null ? distance + call.result.distance : null;
        tailRepaired = true;
      }
    }
    if (firstMatched > 0 && firstMatched >= MIN_REPAIR_RUN) {
      const sub = path.slice(0, firstMatched + 1);
      const call = await callSnap(apiKey, sub, Math.min(MAX_RADIUS_M, radiusUsedM * 2.5), mode);
      attempts++;
      if (call.ok && call.result.coordinates.length >= 2) {
        coordinates = call.result.coordinates.concat(coordinates);
        snappedPoints = call.result.snappedPoints
          .filter((p) => p.originalIndex < firstMatched)
          .concat(snappedPoints);
        distance = distance != null && call.result.distance != null ? distance + call.result.distance : null;
        headRepaired = true;
      }
    }
  }
  if (distance == null && coordinates.length >= 2) distance = Math.round(pathLength(coordinates));

  const finalMatched = new Set(snappedPoints.map((p) => p.originalIndex));
  const unmatchedIndices: number[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < path.length; i++) if (!finalMatched.has(i)) unmatchedIndices.push(i);
  const startOk =
    coordinates.length > 0 && haversineM(coordinates[0], path[0]) <= COMPLETE_TOLERANCE_M;
  const endOk =
    coordinates.length > 0 &&
    haversineM(coordinates[coordinates.length - 1], path[path.length - 1]) <= COMPLETE_TOLERANCE_M;

  const out: SnapResponse = {
    coordinates,
    snappedPoints,
    distance,
    radiusUsedM,
    attempts,
    coverage: {
      sent: path.length,
      matched: finalMatched.size,
      unmatchedIndices,
      headRepaired,
      tailRepaired,
      partial: !(startOk && endOk),
    },
    countryCode: primary.countryCode,
  };
  return NextResponse.json(out);
}

/** Encode [lng, lat] pairs as a Google-style polyline (precision 5 or 6). */
export function encodePolyline(coords: LngLat[], precision: 5 | 6 = 5): string {
  const factor = Math.pow(10, precision);
  const encodeValue = (v: number): string => {
    let value = v < 0 ? ~(v << 1) : v << 1;
    let out = "";
    while (value >= 0x20) {
      out += String.fromCharCode((0x20 | (value & 0x1f)) + 63);
      value >>= 5;
    }
    out += String.fromCharCode(value + 63);
    return out;
  };
  let prevLat = 0;
  let prevLng = 0;
  let out = "";
  for (const [lng, lat] of coords) {
    const iLat = Math.round(lat * factor);
    const iLng = Math.round(lng * factor);
    out += encodeValue(iLat - prevLat) + encodeValue(iLng - prevLng);
    prevLat = iLat;
    prevLng = iLng;
  }
  return out;
}

def dens(pts,gap):
    out=[pts[0]]
    for a,b in zip(pts,pts[1:]):
        d=math.hypot((b[0]-a[0])*111e3,(b[1]-a[1])*111e3*math.cos(math.radians(a[0])))

def run(name,p,rad=40):

  const nearestPathIndex = (pt: LngLat): number => {
    let best = 0;
    let bestD = Infinity;
    for (let i = 0; i < path.length; i++) {
      const d = haversineM(path[i], pt);
      if (d < bestD) {
        bestD = d;
        best = i;
      }
    }
    return best;
  };

  if (coordinates.length >= 2 && matchedIdx.length) {
    const geomEnd = coordinates[coordinates.length - 1];
    const geomStart = coordinates[0];
    const endIdx = Math.min(matchedIdx[matchedIdx.length - 1], nearestPathIndex(geomEnd));
    const startIdx = Math.max(matchedIdx[0], nearestPathIndex(geomStart));
    const repairRadius = Math.min(MAX_RADIUS_M, radiusUsedM * 2.5);

    const tailMissing = path.length - 1 - endIdx;
    if (
      tailMissing >= 1 &&
      (tailMissing >= MIN_REPAIR_RUN || haversineM(geomEnd, path[path.length - 1]) > COMPLETE_TOLERANCE_M)
    ) {
      const sub = path.slice(endIdx);
      const call = await callSnap(apiKey, sub, repairRadius, mode);
      attempts++;
      if (call.ok && call.result.coordinates.length >= 2) {
        coordinates = coordinates.concat(call.result.coordinates);
        snappedPoints = snappedPoints
          .filter((p) => p.originalIndex <= endIdx)
          .concat(
            call.result.snappedPoints
              .filter((p) => p.originalIndex > 0)
              .map((p) => ({ ...p, originalIndex: p.originalIndex + endIdx })),
          );
        distance =
          distance != null && call.result.distance != null ? distance + call.result.distance : null;
        tailRepaired = true;
      }
    }
    if (
      startIdx >= 1 &&
      (startIdx >= MIN_REPAIR_RUN || haversineM(geomStart, path[0]) > COMPLETE_TOLERANCE_M)
    ) {
      const sub = path.slice(0, startIdx + 1);
      const call = await callSnap(apiKey, sub, repairRadius, mode);
      attempts++;
      if (call.ok && call.result.coordinates.length >= 2) {
        coordinates = call.result.coordinates.concat(coordinates);
        snappedPoints = call.result.snappedPoints
          .filter((p) => p.originalIndex < startIdx)
          .concat(snappedPoints.filter((p) => p.originalIndex >= startIdx));
        distance =
          distance != null && call.result.distance != null ? distance + call.result.distance : null;
        headRepaired = true;
      }
    }

  geometry, snapped points, distance, `coverage` (matched/unmatched points,
  whether stitching happened, `partial` flag) and `countryCode`.
- **Export**: `Export GeoJSON` (snapped line, drawn line, control vertices,
  waypoints, snapped points) and `Copy polyline` / `Copy polyline6` (snapped
  route as a Google-encoded polyline on the clipboard).
- The panel shows "Points matched x/y" and an amber warning when the route
  could only be partially matched.""")
s=s.replace("""Auth gate, login route and map proxy follow""","""## Deploy (Cloud Run, GCP project `[GCP_PROJECT]`)

`terraform/` follows the shared `/nb-cloud-run-deploy` layout (Artifact
Registry repo `london-councils`, service `london-councils-demo`, NB key in
Secret Manager `london-councils-demo-nb-api-key`, public ingress with the
app-level login gate).

```bash
cd LONDON_COUNCILS/terraform
cp terraform.tfvars.example terraform.tfvars   # set nb_api_key (gitignored)
terraform init && terraform apply              # APIs, repo, secret, placeholder service

# Build + push from LONDON_COUNCILS/ (uses .gcloudignore; terraform/ is excluded)
cd .. && TAG=$(date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
IMG=us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/[GCP_PROJECT]/london-councils/london-councils-demo:$TAG
gcloud builds submit --tag $IMG --project [GCP_PROJECT]

cd terraform && terraform apply -auto-approve -var image=$IMG
terraform output service_url
```

Always pass `-var image=...` on later applies — the `image` variable defaults
to GCP's hello sample and would otherwise reset the service.

Auth gate, login route and map proxy follow""")
open(p,"w").write(s)
EOF
echo ok
```

### CLAUDE (2026-08-17T13:21:44.647Z)

Done — the three new PRD items are implemented, and I've hardened the snap pipeline against the truncated-route symptom you saw. Production build is clean.

**Partial snap (your screenshot)**
- I could not make NB truncate a route in ~15 probes against `snapToRoads` (long routes, out-of-order waypoints, river/park outliers, re-snap through edited vertices with 12 waypoints — all reached the end), so I couldn't confirm the root cause from a synthetic repro. What NB *does* do is silently drop points it can't fit (`tolerate_outlier`); if a dropped run is at the head or tail, the geometry just stops short — which is exactly what your map shows (69/79 points matched, blue line ends at Shoreditch, drawn tail continues to Bermondsey).
- Fix in `/api/snap`: after the primary call it checks where the returned geometry actually starts/ends relative to the input path; if a leading/trailing run is missing (≥2 points, or the geometry end is >400 m from the path end) it re-snaps that run separately at 2.5× radius and stitches it on. The response now carries `coverage` (`sent`, `matched`, `unmatchedIndices`, `headRepaired`, `tailRepaired`, `partial`).
- UI: the stats show **Points matched x/y (stitched)**, and an amber **"Route only partially matched"** warning with a re-snap link appears whenever the geometry still doesn't reach both ends. If it happens again, that line will tell us immediately whether NB dropped the tail (and the GeoJSON export will contain the exact vertices/waypoints so I can reproduce it).

**New PRD items**
- `detail=true` is now on every snapToRoads request; `country_code` is passed through as `countryCode`.
- **Copy polyline** / **Copy polyline6** buttons copy the snapped route as a Google-encoded polyline to the clipboard (falls back to a textarea copy where the Clipboard API is blocked). Encoder verified against the Google reference vector and round-tripped through the decoder.
- **Terraform for Cloud Run** in `LONDON_COUNCILS/terraform/` (validated with `terraform validate`): project `[GCP_PROJECT]`, Artifact Registry `london-councils`, service `london-councils-demo`, NB key in Secret Manager as `NB_API_KEY`, public ingress + app login gate — same shape as GLWAS. Also added the multi-stage `Dockerfile` (no data dir), a `.gcloudignore` that excludes `terraform/`, and a local `terraform.tfvars` (git-ignored, project + key pre-filled). Deploy steps are in the README. I have **not** run `terraform apply` or built the image — say the word and I'll deploy.

One dev-only addition: the map instance is exposed as `window.__routeSketcherMap` in development builds for scripted testing (stripped in production).

[GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER]). `gcloud` itself also reports "Reauthentication failed … please run `gcloud auth login`", so the user session has hit a re-auth requirement — that's the most likely reason access to `[GCP_PROJECT]` (which worked for the GLWAS deploy earlier today) is now being refused.

start=s.index("  // ---- freehand drawing ---------------------------------------------------")
end=s.index("  }, [mapReady, snap]);")+len("  }, [mapReady, snap]);")
new='''  // ---- click-to-place drawing ---------------------------------------------
  // In draw mode each click places a vertex; a rubber-band segment follows the
  // cursor from the last vertex; double-click (or Enter / the Finish button)
  // completes the route and triggers snapping. Backspace removes the last
  // vertex; Esc cancels.
  const finishDrawing = useCallback(() => {
    const s = strokeRef.current;
    strokeRef.current = null;
    setSource("draft-cursor", lineFC([]));
    if (!s || s.length < 2) {
      setDrawnPath([]);
      setStatus("idle");
      setDrawMode(false);
      return;
    }
    setDrawnPath(s);
    setControlPoints(null);
    setEditMode(false);
    setDrawMode(false);
    void snap(s, { radiusM: radiusRef.current, mode: modeRef.current, source: "stroke" });
  }, [snap, setSource]);
  const finishDrawingRef = useRef(finishDrawing);
  useEffect(() => {
    finishDrawingRef.current = finishDrawing;
  }, [finishDrawing]);

  const undoLastVertex = useCallback(() => {
    const s = strokeRef.current;
    if (!s || !s.length) return;
    s.pop();
    setDrawnPath(s.slice());
    if (!s.length) setStatus("drawing");
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => {
    const map = mapRef.current;
    if (!map || !mapReady) return;

    const placeVertex = (lngLat: maplibregl.LngLat, point: maplibregl.Point) => {
      if (!strokeRef.current) {
        // First vertex of a new route: reset any previous result.
        strokeRef.current = [];
        setResult(null);
        setControlPoints(null);
        setEditMode(false);
        setError(null);
        setStatus("drawing");
      }
      const s = strokeRef.current;
      const last = s[s.length - 1];
      // Ignore a click on top of the previous vertex (e.g. the 2nd click of a
      // double-click) so it doesn't create a duplicate.
      if (last) {
        const lp = map.project(last as [number, number]);
        if (Math.hypot(lp.x - point.x, lp.y - point.y) < 6) return;
      }
      s.push([lngLat.lng, lngLat.lat]);
      setDrawnPath(s.slice());
    };

    const onClick = (e: maplibregl.MapMouseEvent) => {
      if (!drawModeRef.current) return;
      placeVertex(e.lngLat, e.point);
    };
    const onDblClick = (e: maplibregl.MapMouseEvent) => {
      if (!drawModeRef.current) return;
      e.preventDefault();
      // The double-click's own clicks already placed the final vertex.
      finishDrawingRef.current();
    };
    const onMouseMove = (e: maplibregl.MapMouseEvent) => {
      if (!drawModeRef.current) return;
      const s = strokeRef.current;
      if (!s || !s.length) return;
      const last = s[s.length - 1];
      setSource("draft-cursor", lineFC([last, [e.lngLat.lng, e.lngLat.lat]]));
    };
    const onMouseOut = () => setSource("draft-cursor", lineFC([]));

    map.on("click", onClick);
    map.on("dblclick", onDblClick);
    map.on("mousemove", onMouseMove);
    map.on("mouseout", onMouseOut);
    return () => {
      map.off("click", onClick);
      map.off("dblclick", onDblClick);
      map.off("mousemove", onMouseMove);
      map.off("mouseout", onMouseOut);
    };
  }, [mapReady, setSource]);'''
s=s[:start]+new+s[end:]

def rep(a,b):
    global s
    assert s.count(a)==1, a[:70]
    s=s.replace(a,b)

# draft-cursor source/layer + draft vertices layer
rep('''      // Snapped route
      map.addSource("snapped", { type: "geojson", data: lineFC([]) });''','''      // Rubber-band segment from the last placed vertex to the cursor
      map.addSource("draft-cursor", { type: "geojson", data: lineFC([]) });
      map.addLayer({

        source: "draft-cursor",
        layout: { "line-cap": "round" },
        paint: { "line-color": "#f97316", "line-width": 2, "line-opacity": 0.6, "line-dasharray": [2, 2] },
      });
      // Placed vertices of the sketch
      map.addSource("drawn-vertices", { type: "geojson", data: pointFC([]) });
      map.addLayer({

        type: "circle",
        source: "drawn-vertices",
        paint: {
          "circle-radius": 5,
          "circle-color": "#fff",
          "circle-stroke-color": "#f97316",
          "circle-stroke-width": 2,
        },
      });
      // Snapped route
      map.addSource("snapped", { type: "geojson", data: lineFC([]) });''')
rep('''    setSource("drawn", lineFC(drawnPath));
  }, [drawnPath, mapReady, setSource]);''','''    setSource("drawn", lineFC(drawnPath));
    setSource("drawn-vertices", pointFC(drawnPath.map(([lng, lat], i) => ({ lng, lat, index: i }))));
  }, [drawnPath, mapReady, setSource]);''')

# draw mode effect: keep pan enabled, disable dblclick zoom; cancel discards draft
rep('''    if (drawMode) {
      setEditMode(false);

      map.getCanvas().style.cursor = "crosshair";
    } else {
      map.dragPan.enable();

    }
  }, [drawMode, mapReady]);''','''    if (drawMode) {
      setEditMode(false);
      map.doubleClickZoom.disable();
      map.getCanvas().style.cursor = "crosshair";
    } else {
      // Leaving draw mode with an unfinished draft discards it.

        setDrawnPath([]);
        setSource("draft-cursor", lineFC([]));
        setStatus((st) => (st === "drawing" ? "idle" : st));
      }
      if (!editModeRef.current) map.doubleClickZoom.enable();
      map.getCanvas().style.cursor = "";
    }
  }, [drawMode, mapReady, setSource]);''')

rep('''      else if (e.key === "Delete" || e.key === "Backspace") clearAll();''','''      else if (e.key === "Enter" && drawModeRef.current && strokeRef.current) finishDrawingRef.current();

**Draw method change** (`DEMO_PRD.md` last line) — implemented and tested in the browser before building:
- Draw mode is now click-to-place: each click adds a vertex (orange ring), a dashed rubber-band segment follows the cursor from the last vertex, **double-click** finishes (the double-click's own click is de-duplicated so no stray vertex), then the route snaps. Also: Enter or a **Finish** button completes, **Undo**/Backspace removes the last vertex, Esc cancels and discards the draft; the map stays pannable while drawing. [tool: Bash — Add navigate API route]
```bash
cd /Users/[USER]/workspace/poc_data/LONDON_COUNCILS/demo; mkdir -p src/app/api/navigate; cat > src/app/api/navigate/route.ts <<'EOF'
import { NextResponse } from "next/server";
import { decodePolyline, type LngLat } from "@/lib/geometry";

const NB_NAV_URL = "https://api.nextbillion.io/navigation/json";

export interface NavStep {
  index: number;
  instruction: string;
  maneuverType: string;
  modifier?: string;
  distanceM: number;
  durationSec: number;
  name?: string;
  reference?: string;
  /** [lng, lat] of the maneuver point. */
  location: LngLat;
  voice: string[];
}

export interface NavigateResponse {
  distanceM: number;
  durationSec: number;
  steps: NavStep[];
  /** Route geometry returned by the navigation service, [lng, lat] pairs. */
  coordinates: LngLat[];
}

interface NavigateRequestBody {
  /** Encoded polyline of the snapped route. */
  polyline: string;
  precision?: 5 | 6;
  lang?: string;
}

/**
 * Turn-by-turn instructions for an existing route geometry. NB's Navigation
 * API accepts the route shape directly via `original_shape` (POST — the
 * encoded polyline is far too long for a GET query string).
 */
export async function POST(request: Request) {
  const apiKey = process.env.NB_API_KEY;
  if (!apiKey) {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: "NB_API_KEY not configured" }, { status: 500 });
  }
  let body: NavigateRequestBody;
  try {
    body = await request.json();
  } catch {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: "invalid JSON body" }, { status: 400 });
  }
  if (typeof body.polyline !== "string" || body.polyline.length < 4) {
    return NextResponse.json({ error: "polyline required" }, { status: 400 });
  }
  const shapeType = body.precision === 5 ? "polyline" : "polyline6";
  const lang = typeof body.lang === "string" && /^[a-zA-Z-]{2,10}$/.test(body.lang) ? body.lang : "en-GB";

  const r = await fetch(`${NB_NAV_URL}?key=${encodeURIComponent(apiKey)}`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      original_shape: body.polyline,
      original_shape_type: shapeType,
      geometry: "polyline6",
      lang,
    }),
  });
  const text = await r.text();
  let data: any;
  try {
    data = JSON.parse(text);
  } catch {
    return NextResponse.json(
      { error: `non-JSON from NB (${r.status}): ${text.slice(0, 200)}` },
      { status: 502 },
    );
  }
  const statusOk = !data?.status || String(data.status).toLowerCase() === "ok";
  const route = data?.routes?.[0];
  if (!r.ok || !statusOk || !route) {
    return NextResponse.json(
      {
        error: data?.msg ?? data?.message ?? data?.error ?? `navigation failed (${r.status})`,
        raw: data,
      },
      { status: r.ok ? 502 : r.status },
    );
  }

  const steps: NavStep[] = [];
  let idx = 0;
  for (const leg of route.legs ?? []) {
    for (const st of leg.steps ?? []) {
      const m = st?.maneuver ?? {};
      const c = m.coordinate ?? st.start_location ?? {};
      steps.push({
        index: idx++,
        instruction: String(m.instruction ?? ""),
        maneuverType: String(m.maneuver_type ?? m.type ?? ""),
        modifier: m.modifier ? String(m.modifier) : undefined,
        distanceM: Number(st?.distance?.value ?? st?.distance ?? 0),
        durationSec: Number(st?.duration?.value ?? st?.duration ?? 0),
        name: st?.name || undefined,
        reference: st?.reference || undefined,
        location: [Number(c.longitude), Number(c.latitude)],
        voice: Array.isArray(m.voice_instruction)
          ? m.voice_instruction.map((v: any) => String(v?.instruction ?? "")).filter(Boolean)
          : [],
      });
    }
  }
  const coordinates =
    typeof route.geometry === "string" ? decodePolyline(route.geometry, 6) : [];

  const out: NavigateResponse = {
    distanceM: Number(route.distance ?? 0),
    durationSec: Number(route.duration ?? 0),
    steps,
    coordinates,
  };
  return NextResponse.json(out);
}
EOF

/** Compact glyph for a maneuver, keyed on NB's maneuver_type + modifier. */
function maneuverGlyph(type: string, modifier?: string): string {
  const t = type.toLowerCase();
  const mod = (modifier ?? "").toLowerCase();
  if (t === "depart") return "●";
  if (t === "arrive") return "⚑";
  if (t.includes("roundabout") || t.includes("rotary")) return "↻";
  if (t === "merge") return "⤵";
  if (t === "fork" || t.includes("ramp") || t === "on ramp" || t === "off ramp") return "⑂";
  if (t === "uturn" || mod.includes("uturn")) return "⤶";
  if (mod.includes("sharp left")) return "↰";
  if (mod.includes("sharp right")) return "↱";
  if (mod.includes("slight left")) return "↖";
  if (mod.includes("slight right")) return "↗";
  if (mod.includes("left")) return "←";
  if (mod.includes("right")) return "→";
  if (t === "continue" || t === "new name" || mod.includes("straight")) return "↑";
  return "•";
}

### CLAUDE (2026-08-17T13:49:30.038Z)

Implemented, verified, and deployed the new PRD item (Navigate → maneuver instructions).

**How it works**
- After a snap, a green **Navigate** button is enabled (next to "+ Add waypoint"). It encodes the snapped geometry as polyline6 and POSTs it to the new `/api/navigate` route, which calls NB's Navigation API with `original_shape` / `original_shape_type=polyline6` (`lang=en-GB`, `geometry=polyline6`). I used POST because a full-resolution route polyline is ~9 KB and the GET form returned `414 Request-URI Too Large`.
- The response is normalized to steps `{instruction, maneuverType, modifier, distanceM, durationSec, name, reference, location, voice[]}` plus total distance/duration and the nav geometry.
- A **Directions** side panel (top-right) lists every maneuver with a glyph per type (turn arrows, roundabout, merge, depart/arrive…), instruction, distance/duration and road ref; header shows totals + step count, with Refresh and close. Maneuver points are drawn on the map (green dots); clicking a step zooms to it and highlights it red. Instructions are invalidated automatically when the route changes; the button then reads "Navigate" again (or "Show directions" to reopen a still-valid panel).

**Verified in the browser**: click-placed 3-vertex route → snap (21.7 km) → Navigate → 136 steps ("Head southeast on Abbey Road (B507)", "Turn left onto Boundary Road", …) → clicking step 11 focused the map on that turn.

**Deployed**: image `london-councils-demo:20260817-134736` is live at https://london-councils-demo-7j5cx7inrq-uc.a.run.app; the live `/api/navigate` returned 138 steps for a 29.5 km test route through the Secret-Manager-backed key. README updated.

### CLAUDE (2026-08-17T13:54:11.479Z)

Done — the map now uses the NextBillion-proxied TomTom `basic_main` style, and it's deployed.

- `MAP_STYLE` → `/api/map-proxy/tt/style/1/style/25.2.3-0?map=basic_main`. The existing same-origin proxy handles it unchanged: the style's embedded tile (`/tt/map/1/tile/basic/main/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf`), glyph (`/tt/style/1/glyph/…`) and sprite (`/tt/style/1/sprite/…?map=basic_main`) URLs are rewritten to the proxy with the embedded key stripped and the real key attached server-side; verified all four asset types return 200 (locally and against the live service).

- Rendered check in the browser: TomTom basemap draws (roads, shields, water, parks); route/vertex/waypoint/maneuver overlays are unchanged.
- Live: image `london-councils-demo:20260817-135258` at https://london-councils-demo-7j5cx7inrq-uc.a.run.app; the live proxied style rewrites tiles to the service origin and a live tile fetch returns 200. README updated.

  radiusM: number;
  drawnPath: LngLat[];
  controlPoints: Vertex[] | null;
  result: SnapResult;
}

// Phase 1: browser storage. Bump the version if the shape changes.
const STORAGE_KEY = "london_councils.saved_routes.v1";
const CHANGE_EVENT = "london_councils:saved-routes-changed";

function canUseStorage(): boolean {
  try {
    return typeof window !== "undefined" && !!window.localStorage;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

export function listSavedRoutes(): SavedRoute[] {
  if (!canUseStorage()) return [];
  try {
    const raw = window.localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY);
    if (!raw) return [];
    const parsed = JSON.parse(raw);
    if (!Array.isArray(parsed)) return [];
    return parsed
      .filter(
        (r): r is SavedRoute =>
          r &&
          typeof r.id === "string" &&
          typeof r.name === "string" &&
          Array.isArray(r.drawnPath) &&
          r.result &&
          Array.isArray(r.result.coordinates),
      )
      .sort((a, b) => (a.updatedAt < b.updatedAt ? 1 : -1));
  } catch {
    return [];
  }
}

function writeAll(routes: SavedRoute[]): void {
  window.localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, JSON.stringify(routes));
  window.dispatchEvent(new Event(CHANGE_EVENT));
}

export function newRouteId(): string {
  return typeof crypto !== "undefined" && "randomUUID" in crypto
    ? crypto.randomUUID()
    : `${Date.now().toString(36)}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 10)}`;
}

/** Insert or replace (by id). Returns the stored record. */
export function saveRoute(route: SavedRoute): SavedRoute {
  const all = listSavedRoutes().filter((r) => r.id !== route.id);
  all.unshift(route);
  writeAll(all);
  return route;
}

export function renameRoute(id: string, name: string): void {
  const all = listSavedRoutes().map((r) =>
    r.id === id ? { ...r, name, updatedAt: new Date().toISOString() } : r,
  );
  writeAll(all);
}

export function deleteRoute(id: string): void {
  writeAll(listSavedRoutes().filter((r) => r.id !== id));
}

/** Subscribe to changes (same tab via custom event, other tabs via `storage`). */
export function onSavedRoutesChange(cb: () => void): () => void {
  if (!canUseStorage()) return () => {};
  const onStorage = (e: StorageEvent) => {
    if (e.key === null || e.key === STORAGE_KEY) cb();
  };
  window.addEventListener(CHANGE_EVENT, cb);
  window.addEventListener("storage", onStorage);
  return () => {
    window.removeEventListener(CHANGE_EVENT, cb);
    window.removeEventListener("storage", onStorage);
  };
}

cd /Users/[USER]/workspace/poc_data/LONDON_COUNCILS/demo; cat > src/lib/permit-pdf.ts <<'EOF'
import { jsPDF } from "jspdf";
import type { NavigateResponse } from "@/app/api/navigate/route";
import type { Vertex } from "@/lib/saved-routes";

export interface PermitInput {
  routeName: string;
  mode: "car" | "truck";
  snappedDistanceM: number | null;
  nav: NavigateResponse;
  waypoints: Array<Vertex & { wp: NonNullable<Vertex["wp"]> }>;
  /** Optional PNG data URL of the map view to embed on page 1. */
  mapImageDataUrl?: string | null;
  encodedPolyline: string;
}

function fmtKm(m: number | null | undefined): string {
  if (m == null || !Number.isFinite(m)) return "—";
  return m >= 1000 ? `${(m / 1000).toFixed(2)} km` : `${Math.round(m)} m`;
}
function fmtDuration(sec: number): string {
  const m = Math.round(sec / 60);
  return m < 60 ? `${m} min` : `${Math.floor(m / 60)} h ${m % 60} min`;
}

/**
 * Builds the "Route Permit" PDF: header block, summary, optional map snapshot,
 * waypoints, then the full numbered maneuver list (paginated). Returns the
 * jsPDF document; caller decides whether to save or open it.
 */
export function buildPermitPdf(input: PermitInput): jsPDF {
  const doc = new jsPDF({ unit: "mm", format: "a4" });
  const pageW = doc.internal.pageSize.getWidth();
  const pageH = doc.internal.pageSize.getHeight();
  const margin = 15;
  const contentW = pageW - margin * 2;
  let y = margin;
  const generated = new Date();
  const permitRef = `LC-${generated.toISOString().slice(0, 10).replace(/-/g, "")}-${Math.random()
    .toString(36)
    .slice(2, 6)
    .toUpperCase()}`;

  const footer = () => {
    const n = doc.getNumberOfPages();
    for (let i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
      doc.setPage(i);
      doc.setFontSize(8);
      doc.setTextColor(120);
      doc.text(`Route permit ${permitRef} · ${input.routeName} · page ${i} of ${n}`, margin, pageH - 8);
      doc.text("Routing by NextBillion.ai", pageW - margin, pageH - 8, { align: "right" });
    }
    doc.setTextColor(0);
  };
  const ensureSpace = (needed: number) => {
    if (y + needed > pageH - margin - 6) {
      doc.addPage();
      y = margin;
    }
  };

  // ---- header --------------------------------------------------------------
  doc.setFillColor(15, 61, 145);
  doc.rect(0, 0, pageW, 22, "F");
  doc.setTextColor(255);
  doc.setFont("helvetica", "bold");
  doc.setFontSize(16);
  doc.text("Route Permit", margin, 14);
  doc.setFont("helvetica", "normal");
  doc.setFontSize(10);
  doc.text("London Councils — Route Permit Generator", pageW - margin, 14, { align: "right" });
  doc.setTextColor(0);
  y = 30;

  doc.setFont("helvetica", "bold");
  doc.setFontSize(13);
  doc.text(input.routeName, margin, y);
  y += 7;
  doc.setFont("helvetica", "normal");
  doc.setFontSize(9.5);
  const summary: Array<[string, string]> = [
    ["Permit reference", permitRef],
    ["Generated", generated.toLocaleString("en-GB")],
    ["Vehicle profile", input.mode === "truck" ? "Truck" : "Car"],
    ["Route length (navigation)", fmtKm(input.nav.distanceM)],
    ["Estimated driving time", fmtDuration(input.nav.durationSec)],
    ["Snapped route length", fmtKm(input.snappedDistanceM)],
    ["Maneuvers", String(input.nav.steps.length)],
    ["Waypoints", String(input.waypoints.length)],
  ];
  for (const [k, v] of summary) {
    doc.setTextColor(90);
    doc.text(k, margin, y);
    doc.setTextColor(0);
    doc.text(v, margin + 55, y);
    y += 5.2;
  }
  y += 2;

  // ---- map snapshot --------------------------------------------------------
  if (input.mapImageDataUrl) {
    try {
      const props = doc.getImageProperties(input.mapImageDataUrl);
      const maxH = 80;
      let w = contentW;
      let h = (props.height / props.width) * w;
      if (h > maxH) {
        h = maxH;
        w = (props.width / props.height) * h;
      }
      ensureSpace(h + 4);
      doc.addImage(input.mapImageDataUrl, "PNG", margin, y, w, h);
      doc.setDrawColor(200);
      doc.rect(margin, y, w, h);
      y += h + 6;
    } catch {
      // Snapshot is optional — skip silently if the canvas couldn't be read.
    }
  }

  // ---- waypoints -----------------------------------------------------------
  if (input.waypoints.length) {
    ensureSpace(12);
    doc.setFont("helvetica", "bold");
    doc.setFontSize(11);
    doc.text("Waypoints (in route order)", margin, y);
    y += 6;
    doc.setFont("helvetica", "normal");
    doc.setFontSize(9.5);
    input.waypoints.forEach((v, i) => {
      ensureSpace(5.5);
      doc.text(`${i + 1}. ${v.wp.label}  (${v.pos[1].toFixed(5)}, ${v.pos[0].toFixed(5)})`, margin + 2, y);
      y += 5.2;
    });
    y += 3;
  }

  // ---- maneuvers -----------------------------------------------------------
  ensureSpace(14);
  doc.setFont("helvetica", "bold");
  doc.setFontSize(11);
  doc.text("Turn-by-turn instructions", margin, y);
  y += 6;

  const colNo = margin;
  const colInstr = margin + 10;
  const colDist = pageW - margin - 40;
  const colDur = pageW - margin - 18;
  const instrW = colDist - colInstr - 3;

  const header = () => {
    doc.setFillColor(235, 238, 245);
    doc.rect(margin, y - 4, contentW, 6, "F");
    doc.setFont("helvetica", "bold");
    doc.setFontSize(8.5);
    doc.text("#", colNo + 1, y);
    doc.text("Instruction", colInstr, y);
    doc.text("Distance", colDist, y);
    doc.text("Time", colDur, y);
    y += 5;
    doc.setFont("helvetica", "normal");
    doc.setFontSize(9);
  };
  header();

  let cumulative = 0;
  input.nav.steps.forEach((st, i) => {
    const lines = doc.splitTextToSize(st.instruction || st.maneuverType, instrW) as string[];
    const road = st.name ? `${st.name}${st.reference ? ` (${st.reference})` : ""}` : st.reference ?? "";
    const rowH = lines.length * 4.2 + (road ? 3.8 : 0) + 2.5;
    if (y + rowH > pageH - margin - 6) {
      doc.addPage();
      y = margin;
      header();
    }
    if (i % 2 === 1) {
      doc.setFillColor(248, 249, 251);
      doc.rect(margin, y - 3.6, contentW, rowH, "F");
    }
    doc.setTextColor(0);
    doc.text(String(i + 1), colNo + 1, y);
    doc.text(lines, colInstr, y);
    doc.text(st.distanceM > 0 ? fmtKm(st.distanceM) : "—", colDist, y);
    doc.text(st.durationSec > 0 ? fmtDuration(st.durationSec) : "—", colDur, y);
    let yy = y + lines.length * 4.2;
    if (road) {
      doc.setTextColor(110);
      doc.setFontSize(8);
      doc.text(`${road} · ${fmtKm(cumulative)} from start`, colInstr, yy - 0.5);
      doc.setFontSize(9);
      doc.setTextColor(0);
      yy += 3.8;
    }
    cumulative += st.distanceM;
    y = yy + 2.5;
  });

  // ---- appendix: encoded polyline -----------------------------------------
  ensureSpace(20);
  y += 4;
  doc.setFont("helvetica", "bold");
  doc.setFontSize(10);
  doc.text("Route geometry (encoded polyline, precision 5)", margin, y);
  y += 5;
  doc.setFont("courier", "normal");
  doc.setFontSize(6.5);
  const polyLines = doc.splitTextToSize(input.encodedPolyline, contentW) as string[];
  for (const ln of polyLines) {
    ensureSpace(3.2);
    doc.text(ln, margin, y);
    y += 3.0;
  }
  doc.setFont("helvetica", "normal");

  footer();
  return doc;
}
EOF

### CLAUDE (2026-08-17T15:04:36.687Z)

Both new PRD items are implemented; production build is clean. Not deployed yet — say the word and I'll build the image and roll it out (your title/branding edits to `layout.tsx` / `login/page.tsx` — "Route Permit Generator" — will ship with it).

**Saved routes** (phase 1: browser `localStorage`)
- New `src/lib/saved-routes.ts` stores `{id, name, createdAt, updatedAt, mode, radiusM, drawnPath, controlPoints (incl. waypoints), result}` under `london_councils.saved_routes.v1`, with list/save/rename/delete and a change-subscription (same tab + cross-tab `storage` events).
- Panel section **Saved routes (n)**: name field + **Save as new** (enabled once a route is snapped); a list (newest first) showing name, length, waypoint count, timestamp with **Load / Rename / Delete** (Delete asks Yes/No inline). Loading restores the sketch, vertices, waypoints, snap result, profile and radius, zooms to the route and shows "Working on *name*"; further edits flag "unsaved changes" and enable **Update** to overwrite. Starting a new sketch or Clear detaches from the saved record.
- Verified in the browser: saved "West End test" → full page reload → still listed → Load restored it → Rename to "West End permit route".

**Generate Permit (PDF)**
- `jspdf` added; `src/lib/permit-pdf.ts` builds an A4 permit: blue header, route name, permit reference (`LC-YYYYMMDD-XXXX`), summary (generated time, profile, nav length, driving time, snapped length, maneuver/waypoint counts), a **map snapshot fitted to the route** (map now created with `preserveDrawingBuffer` so the canvas can be captured), waypoints list, the full numbered turn-by-turn table (instruction, distance, time, road/ref + cumulative distance; zebra rows, repeated header, pagination) and an encoded-polyline appendix; footer with reference/page numbers on every page.
- **Generate Permit (PDF)** button in the main panel (below Navigate) and in the Directions panel header — enabled only after Navigate has returned; saves `route_permit_<name>.pdf`.
- Verified by building the PDF from a real 138-step navigation response in Node (7 pages) and rendering page 1 — layout checks out.

Also folded into `src/lib/saved-routes.ts`: the `Vertex` / `Waypoint` / `SnapResult` types moved out of the component so the storage and PDF modules can share them.

rep('''// TomTom "basic_main" vector style, served through NextBillion.ai (and our proxy).
const MAP_STYLE = "/api/map-proxy/tt/style/1/style/25.2.3-0?map=basic_main";''',
'''// TomTom vector styles served through NextBillion.ai (and our proxy).
const MAP_STYLE = "/api/map-proxy/tt/style/1/style/25.2.3-0?map=basic_main";
// Light street style with the live traffic-incidents overlay, used when the
// traffic toggle is on.
const MAP_STYLE_TRAFFIC =
  "/api/map-proxy/tt/style/1/style/25.2.3-0?map=2/basic_street-light&traffic_incidents=2/incidents_light";
// Sources we add on top of the base style; preserved across style swaps.
const APP_SOURCE_IDS = new Set([
  "drawn",
  "draft-cursor",
  "drawn-vertices",
  "snapped",
  "input-points",
  "snapped-points",
  "endpoints",
  "control-points",
  "waypoints",
  "maneuvers",
]);

/** Minimal MapLibre control: a single toggle button for the traffic layer. */
class TrafficToggleControl implements maplibregl.IControl {
  private container: HTMLDivElement | null = null;
  private button: HTMLButtonElement | null = null;
  private on = false;
  constructor(private readonly onToggle: (next: boolean) => void) {}
  onAdd(): HTMLElement {
    this.container = document.createElement("div");
    this.container.className = "maplibregl-ctrl maplibregl-ctrl-group";
    this.button = document.createElement("button");
    this.button.type = "button";
    this.button.title = "Toggle live traffic incidents";
    this.button.setAttribute("aria-label", "Toggle traffic layer");
    this.button.setAttribute("aria-pressed", "false");
    this.button.style.fontSize = "16px";
    this.button.textContent = "🚦";
    this.button.addEventListener("click", () => this.onToggle(!this.on));
    this.container.appendChild(this.button);
    return this.container;
  }
  onRemove(): void {
    this.container?.remove();
    this.container = null;
    this.button = null;
  }
  setActive(on: boolean): void {
    this.on = on;
    if (!this.button) return;
    this.button.setAttribute("aria-pressed", String(on));
    this.button.style.background = on ? "#fde68a" : "";
    this.button.title = on ? "Hide traffic incidents" : "Show live traffic incidents";
  }
}''')

# state
rep('''  const [mapReady, setMapReady] = useState(false);''','''  const [mapReady, setMapReady] = useState(false);
  const [traffic, setTraffic] = useState(false);
  const trafficCtrlRef = useRef<TrafficToggleControl | null>(null);''')

# add control in map init after NavigationControl
rep('''    map.addControl(new maplibregl.NavigationControl({ showCompass: false }), "top-right");''',
'''    map.addControl(new maplibregl.NavigationControl({ showCompass: false }), "top-right");
    const trafficCtrl = new TrafficToggleControl((next) => setTraffic(next));
    trafficCtrlRef.current = trafficCtrl;
    map.addControl(trafficCtrl, "top-right");''')

# effect: swap style keeping app sources/layers
rep('''  // ---- helpers to push data into sources ----------------------------------''',
'''  // ---- traffic layer toggle (style swap that keeps our overlays) -----------
  useEffect(() => {
    trafficCtrlRef.current?.setActive(traffic);
    const map = mapRef.current;
    if (!map || !mapReady) return;
    const target = traffic ? MAP_STYLE_TRAFFIC : MAP_STYLE;
    map.setStyle(target, {
      diff: false,
      transformStyle: (previous, next) => {
        if (!previous) return next;
        const keptSources: Record<string, unknown> = {};
        for (const [id, src] of Object.entries(previous.sources ?? {})) {
          if (APP_SOURCE_IDS.has(id)) keptSources[id] = src;
        }
        const keptLayers = (previous.layers ?? []).filter(
          (l) => "source" in l && typeof l.source === "string" && APP_SOURCE_IDS.has(l.source),
        );
        return {
          ...next,
          sources: { ...next.sources, ...(keptSources as typeof next.sources) },
          layers: [...next.layers, ...keptLayers],
        };
      },
    });
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [traffic]);

  // ---- helpers to push data into sources ----------------------------------''')
open(p,"w").write(s)
EOF

**What was added**
- A 🚦 **map control** (top-right, below the zoom buttons; amber when active) toggles between the current `basic_main` style and the traffic style you specified: `tt/style/1/style/25.2.3-0?map=2/basic_street-light&traffic_incidents=2/incidents_light` — both loaded through the existing `/api/map-proxy`, which also rewrites the new incident-tile source (`/tt/traffic/map/4/tile/incidents/...`) and the style-specific sprite (verified 200s through the proxy).
- The swap is done with `map.setStyle(url, { transformStyle })`, which re-injects all of the app's own sources and layers (sketch, rubber band, snapped route, vertices, waypoints, maneuvers) into the new style, so nothing you've drawn is lost when toggling. A ref guards against redundant style reloads.

**Verified in the browser**: toggled on → light street basemap with red incident segments across London; drew and snapped a route while traffic was on; toggled off → back to `basic_main` with the route/vertices still on the map.

### CLAUDE (2026-08-17T16:41:58.099Z)

Recommendation: don't fetch or ship image assets — **draw the shields programmatically from a single "shield spec"**, once as inline SVG (React) for the Directions panel and once as vector shapes in jsPDF for the permit. Details:

**1. Classification (one shared function)**
NB's navigation steps already give you `reference` (e.g. `A41`, `M25`, `B507`) and `road_shield_type.label`. Classify by prefix, matching UK signage conventions and the TomTom basemap you're already showing:
- `M\d+` or `A\d+\(M\)` → motorway: white text on blue (#0d3f8f)
- `A\d+` → A-road: yellow text (#ffd400) on green (#0a5f38) — TomTom renders all A-roads green (as in your map), and true primary/non-primary status isn't in the nav response, so green is the consistent choice; if you want, treat 3–4-digit A-roads as non-primary (black on white) as a heuristic
- `B\d+` → black text on white with dark border
- fallback → grey pill
Handle multiple refs (`A1/A41` → two shields) and use `reference` for the row plus, optionally, regex the `(A41)` tokens inside the instruction text to place shields inline.

**2. Directions panel** — a tiny `<Shield ref="A41"/>` component: `<svg>` rounded rect + centered bold text, height ~16px, width scaled to label length. Zero assets, crisp at any DPI, theme-independent.

**3. Permit PDF** — the same spec drives `doc.setFillColor / roundedRect / setTextColor / text` in `permit-pdf.ts`, drawn at the start of each row (after the ETA column). Vector = sharp print and tiny file size; no canvas→PNG round trip needed. (If you ever want pixel-identical icons, the alternative is rasterizing the SVG to PNG via canvas and `addImage`, but it's slower, blurrier and unnecessary here.)

**Not recommended**: pulling shield icons from the TomTom style sprite through the proxy — the sprite is versioned/private, icon names aren't documented, and you'd be coupling the permit to a map style.

Want me to implement it that way (shared `shields.ts` + `<Shield>` + PDF drawing) and add it to both places?

/**
 * UK road-number shields, drawn programmatically (no image assets).
 * One spec drives both the React <Shield> component and the jsPDF renderer.
 */
export type ShieldKind = "motorway" | "a-road" | "b-road" | "other";

export interface ShieldSpec {
  label: string;
  kind: ShieldKind;
  /** Fill / text / border colours as [r, g, b]. */
  fill: [number, number, number];
  text: [number, number, number];
  border: [number, number, number];
}

const PALETTE: Record<ShieldKind, Pick<ShieldSpec, "fill" | "text" | "border">> = {
  // Motorway: white on blue
  motorway: { fill: [13, 63, 143], text: [255, 255, 255], border: [255, 255, 255] },
  // A-road (primary route signage): yellow on green — matches the TomTom basemap
  "a-road": { fill: [10, 95, 56], text: [255, 212, 0], border: [255, 255, 255] },
  // B-road / non-primary: black on white
  "b-road": { fill: [255, 255, 255], text: [17, 24, 39], border: [55, 65, 81] },
  other: { fill: [229, 231, 235], text: [31, 41, 55], border: [156, 163, 175] },
};

export function classifyRoadRef(ref: string): ShieldKind {
  const r = ref.trim().toUpperCase();
  if (/^M\d+/.test(r) || /^A\d+\(M\)/.test(r)) return "motorway";
  if (/^A\d+/.test(r)) return "a-road";
  if (/^B\d+/.test(r)) return "b-road";
  return "other";
}

export function shieldSpec(ref: string): ShieldSpec {
  const label = ref.trim().toUpperCase();
  const kind = classifyRoadRef(label);
  return { label, kind, ...PALETTE[kind] };
}

/**
 * Split a reference string into individual road numbers. NB may return
 * "A1", "A1/A41", "A406;A1" or "M25 (M1)" style values.
 */
export function splitRoadRefs(ref?: string | null): string[] {
  if (!ref) return [];
  const out: string[] = [];
  for (const m of ref.toUpperCase().matchAll(/\b([MAB]\d{1,4}(?:\(M\))?)\b/g)) {
    if (!out.includes(m[1])) out.push(m[1]);
  }
  return out;
}

export function rgbCss([r, g, b]: [number, number, number]): string {
  return `rgb(${r},${g},${b})`;
}
EOF

/** Inline-SVG UK road shield (M/A/B classification by prefix). */
export default function Shield({ refNo, height = 16 }: { refNo: string; height?: number }) {
  const s = shieldSpec(refNo);
  const fontSize = height * 0.68;
  const width = Math.max(height * 1.4, s.label.length * fontSize * 0.62 + height * 0.5);
  return (
    <svg
      width={width}
      height={height}
      viewBox={`0 0 ${width} ${height}`}
      role="img"
      aria-label={`Road ${s.label}`}
      className="inline-block align-middle shrink-0"
    >
      <rect
        x={0.75}
        y={0.75}
        width={width - 1.5}
        height={height - 1.5}
        rx={height * 0.2}
        fill={rgbCss(s.fill)}
        stroke={rgbCss(s.border)}
        strokeWidth={1.5}
      />
      <text
        x={width / 2}
        y={height / 2}
        dominantBaseline="central"
        textAnchor="middle"
        fontFamily="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif"
        fontWeight={700}
        fontSize={fontSize}
        fill={rgbCss(s.text)}
      >
        {s.label}
      </text>
    </svg>
  );
}

### CLAUDE (2026-08-17T17:53:30.902Z)

Yes — the shields are ordinary symbol layers in the style (121 layers, ids `Shield<road class><0|1|2>`, `symbol-placement: line`), so we can thin them without touching NB/TomTom: apply a **client-side style transform** in the proxy response or, cleaner, in MapLibre after the style loads (`map.setLayoutProperty` / `setLayerZoomRange`), and it survives the traffic-style swap if done in the same `transformStyle` hook we already use.

Two knobs, in order of effect:

1. **Raise `minzoom` per road class** — this is what your screenshot needs. At London-wide zoom (~10) the style already shows shields for Motorway (minzoom 7), International (6), Major road (8) *and* Secondary road (9) — the A-roads and B-roads packing the view. Bumping e.g. Secondary → 11, Major → 10, Connecting/Major-local → 12–13, and leaving Motorway/International alone gives a Google-like density: at z10 you'd see M25/M1/M11/A1(M)-class only, A-roads appear as you zoom in.
2. **Increase `symbol-spacing`** (currently 200/250/300 px for the `0/1/2` variants) to e.g. 500–800 px so a long road repeats its shield less often, and/or raise `icon-padding` (5 → 20) so MapLibre's collision detection drops more neighbours.

Implementation sketch (one function, ~20 lines, applied to both `basic_main` and the traffic style):

```ts
const SHIELD_MINZOOM: Record<string, number> = {

p="src/components/RouteSketcher.tsx"; s=open(p).read()

"""// Road-shield density: the TomTom style shows shields for A/B roads from
// zoom ~9, which is far too dense at a London-wide view. Raise the minimum
// zoom per road class and repeat shields less often along a road.
const SHIELD_MINZOOM: Record<string, number> = {
  Motorway: 7,
  "International road": 8,
  "Major road": 10,
  "Secondary road": 11,
  "Connecting road": 12,
  "Major local road": 13,
  "Local road": 14,
  "Minor local road": 15,
};
const SHIELD_SPACING_PX = 600;
const SHIELD_PADDING_PX = 20;

function thinShields(style: maplibregl.StyleSpecification): maplibregl.StyleSpecification {
  return {
    ...style,
    layers: style.layers.map((l) => {
      if (!l.id.startsWith("Shield") || l.type !== "symbol") return l;
      const src = "source-layer" in l && typeof l["source-layer"] === "string" ? l["source-layer"] : "";
      const cls = src.replace(/^Toll /, "").replace(/ tunnel$/, "");
      const mz = SHIELD_MINZOOM[cls];
      return {
        ...l,
        ...(mz != null ? { minzoom: Math.max(l.minzoom ?? 0, mz) } : {}),
        layout: {
          ...(l.layout ?? {}),
          "symbol-spacing": SHIELD_SPACING_PX,
          "icon-padding": SHIELD_PADDING_PX,
        },
      };
    }),
  };
}

/** Style transform used on initial load and on every swap: thin the road
 *  shields and carry our own sources/layers across from the previous style. */
function transformBaseStyle(
  previous: maplibregl.StyleSpecification | undefined,
  next: maplibregl.StyleSpecification,
): maplibregl.StyleSpecification {
  const thinned = thinShields(next);
  if (!previous) return thinned;
  const keptSources: Record<string, unknown> = {};
  for (const [id, src] of Object.entries(previous.sources ?? {})) {
    if (APP_SOURCE_IDS.has(id)) keptSources[id] = src;
  }
  const keptLayers = (previous.layers ?? []).filter(
    (l) => "source" in l && typeof l.source === "string" && APP_SOURCE_IDS.has(l.source),
  );
  return {
    ...thinned,
    sources: { ...thinned.sources, ...(keptSources as typeof thinned.sources) },
    layers: [...thinned.layers, ...keptLayers],
  };
}

/** Minimal MapLibre control: a single toggle button for the traffic layer. */""")

# initial load: create without style, then setStyle with transform
rep("""    const map = new maplibregl.Map({
      container: containerRef.current,
      style: MAP_STYLE,
      bounds: LONDON_BOUNDS,""","""    const map = new maplibregl.Map({
      container: containerRef.current,
      bounds: LONDON_BOUNDS,""")
rep("""    map.touchZoomRotate.disableRotation();
    map.dragRotate.disable();
""","""    map.touchZoomRotate.disableRotation();
    map.dragRotate.disable();
    // Load the base style through the same transform used for swaps.
    map.setStyle(MAP_STYLE, { transformStyle: (prev, next) => transformBaseStyle(prev, next) });
""")
# swap: use shared transform
rep("""    map.setStyle(target, {
      diff: false,
      transformStyle: (previous, next) => {
        if (!previous) return next;
        const keptSources: Record<string, unknown> = {};
        for (const [id, src] of Object.entries(previous.sources ?? {})) {
          if (APP_SOURCE_IDS.has(id)) keptSources[id] = src;
        }
        const keptLayers = (previous.layers ?? []).filter(
          (l) => "source" in l && typeof l.source === "string" && APP_SOURCE_IDS.has(l.source),
        );
        return {
          ...next,
          sources: { ...next.sources, ...(keptSources as typeof next.sources) },
          layers: [...next.layers, ...keptLayers],
        };
      },
    });""","""    map.setStyle(target, {
      diff: false,
      transformStyle: (previous, next) => transformBaseStyle(previous, next),
    });""")
open(p,"w").write(s)
EOF
npx tsc --noEmit -p . 2>&1 | head; echo TSC_DONE
```

```bash
cd /Users/[USER]/workspace/poc_data/LONDON_COUNCILS/demo; python3 - <<'EOF'
p="src/components/RouteSketcher.tsx"; s=open(p).read()
a="""function thinShields(style: maplibregl.StyleSpecification): maplibregl.StyleSpecification {
  return {
    ...style,
    layers: style.layers.map((l) => {
      if (!l.id.startsWith("Shield") || l.type !== "symbol") return l;
      const src = "source-layer" in l && typeof l["source-layer"] === "string" ? l["source-layer"] : "";
      const cls = src.replace(/^Toll /, "").replace(/ tunnel$/, "");
      const mz = SHIELD_MINZOOM[cls];
      return {
        ...l,
        ...(mz != null ? { minzoom: Math.max(l.minzoom ?? 0, mz) } : {}),
        layout: {
          ...(l.layout ?? {}),
          "symbol-spacing": SHIELD_SPACING_PX,
          "icon-padding": SHIELD_PADDING_PX,
        },
      };
    }),
  };
}"""
assert s.count(a)==1
s=s.replace(a,"""// The v2 (street-light / traffic) style has a single "roads" source-layer with
// a `category` attribute and a zoom-stepped filter; these are the zooms at
// which each category's shields become visible.
const V2_SHIELD_STEPS: Array<[number, string[]]> = [
  [0, ["motorway", "trunk"]],
  [10, ["motorway", "trunk", "primary"]],
  [12, ["motorway", "trunk", "primary", "secondary"]],
];
const V2_ALL_ROADS_FROM_ZOOM = 14;

function thinShields(style: maplibregl.StyleSpecification): maplibregl.StyleSpecification {
  return {
    ...style,
    layers: style.layers.map((l) => {
      if (l.type !== "symbol") return l;
      const src = "source-layer" in l && typeof l["source-layer"] === "string" ? l["source-layer"] : "";
      const denser = {
        ...(l.layout ?? {}),
        "symbol-spacing": SHIELD_SPACING_PX,
        "icon-padding": SHIELD_PADDING_PX,
      };
      // v1 style (basic_main): one layer per road class, "Shield<Class><n>".
      if (l.id.startsWith("Shield")) {
        const cls = src.replace(/^Toll /, "").replace(/ tunnel$/, "");
        const mz = SHIELD_MINZOOM[cls];
        return { ...l, ...(mz != null ? { minzoom: Math.max(l.minzoom ?? 0, mz) } : {}), layout: denser };
      }
      // v2 style: "TransitLabels - Road Shield n" on the "roads" source-layer.
      if (/Road Shield/i.test(l.id) && src === "roads") {
        const f = l.filter as unknown[] | undefined;
        const hasClause = Array.isArray(f) && f[0] === "all" ? f[1] : undefined;
        const step: unknown[] = ["step", ["zoom"]];
        V2_SHIELD_STEPS.forEach(([z, cats], i) => {
          if (i > 0) step.push(z);
          step.push(["match", ["get", "category"], cats, true, false]);
        });
        step.push(V2_ALL_ROADS_FROM_ZOOM, ["match", ["get", "category"], ["street"], false, true]);
        const filter = hasClause ? ["all", hasClause, step] : ["all", step];
        return { ...l, filter: filter as typeof l.filter, layout: denser };
      }
      return l;
    }),
  };
}""")
open(p,"w").write(s)
EOF

### CLAUDE (2026-08-17T18:09:40.345Z)

Both done and verified in the browser; production build clean (not deployed/committed).

**Shield density** — a `transformBaseStyle()` hook now runs on the initial style load *and* on every traffic toggle swap (it also carries our overlays across, replacing the earlier inline code):
- `basic_main` (v1 style, one `Shield<Class>` layer per road class): raised per-class `minzoom` — Motorway 7, International 8, Major (A) 10, Secondary 11, Connecting 12, Major-local 13, Local 14, Minor-local 15 — plus `symbol-spacing` 600 px and `icon-padding` 20 px.
- The traffic style turned out to be TomTom's v2 schema (a single `roads` source-layer with a `category` attribute and a zoom-stepped filter), so it gets an equivalent rewritten filter: motorway/trunk only until z10, +primary at 10, +secondary at 12, everything at 14.
- Result at London-wide zoom: motorways and main A-roads only, no B-road clutter (screenshots checked for both styles).

**Shield size** — `icon-size` and `text-size` on the same layers are multiplied by **1.25** (numbers scaled directly, expressions wrapped in `["*", expr, 1.25]`), so icon and label grow together.

Say the word for deploy / commit.

done

cat > Dockerfile <<'EOF'
# Multi-stage Dockerfile for the AUTO_CARRIER (ATP) demo.
# Build context: the AUTO_CARRIER/ directory (contains demo/).
#
# The app calls NextBillion.ai from the browser, so the key is baked into the
# client bundle at BUILD time via NEXT_PUBLIC_NB_API_KEY:
#   docker build --platform=linux/amd64 \
#     --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_NB_API_KEY="$NB_KEY" -t IMAGE . && docker push IMAGE

FROM node:20-alpine AS deps
WORKDIR /app
COPY demo/package.json demo/package-lock.json* ./
RUN npm ci

FROM node:20-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /app
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_NB_API_KEY=""
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_NB_API_KEY=${NEXT_PUBLIC_NB_API_KEY}
ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1
COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY demo/ ./
RUN npm run build

FROM node:20-alpine AS runner
WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV=production
ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1
ENV HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0
# Cloud Run sets PORT itself; default for local docker-run.
ENV PORT=8080

RUN addgroup -S app && adduser -S app -G app

# Standalone Next.js server.js + minimal node_modules.
COPY --from=builder --chown=app:app /app/.next/standalone ./
COPY --from=builder --chown=app:app /app/.next/static ./.next/static
COPY --from=builder --chown=app:app /app/public ./public

USER app
EXPOSE 8080
CMD ["node", "server.js"]
EOF
cat > .gcloudignore <<'EOF'
# Controls what `gcloud builds submit` uploads as the build context.
.git
**/node_modules
**/.next
**/.env
**/.env.local
**/*.log
**/.DS_Store
# Never upload terraform state or tfvars (they hold secrets).
terraform
demo/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo
reference
EOF
KEY=$(grep '^NEXT_PUBLIC_NB_API_KEY=' demo/.env.local | cut -d= -f2); cat > terraform/terraform.tfvars <<EOF
project_id = "[GCP_PROJECT]"
region     = "us-central1"
nb_api_key = "$KEY"
EOF
cd terraform && terraform init -backend=false -input=false >/dev/null && terraform validate && cd .. && git -C .. check-ignore -q AUTO_CARRIER/terraform/terraform.tfvars AUTO_CARRIER/demo/.env.local && echo "secrets ignored"
```

### CLAUDE (2026-08-17T19:10:18.289Z)

Found and fixed. Cause: `chooseSlot()` in `src/lib/slots.ts` picked the *deepest* free slot among the cheapest (no-shuffle) candidates. Depth = number of blockers, and slot 7 has two (8, 9) while slot 6 has one (9), so 7 always won over 6 (and 8 over… etc.), giving the fill order 1, 2, 3/4, 5/7, 6/8, 9.

Change: among the no-shuffle candidates, fill in **slot-number order 1 → 9** (that numbering is the carrier's natural front-to-ramp loading sequence and is itself shuffle-free from empty). The same rule now applies when putting shuffled cars back on. Verified with a simulated 9-pickup route: load order is now `1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9` with 0 reshuffles; LIFO-consistent deliveries still unload with 0 reshuffles. Production build passes; not deployed/committed.

One note: slot choice still ignores each car's delivery position (it only avoids shuffles at pickup time). If you'd like, a further improvement is to place cars by delivery order (last-delivered deepest) using the known manifest, which would cut reshuffles on non-LIFO routes — say the word.

GET /api/geocode?q=...\n */\nexport async function GET(request: Request) {\n  const apiKey = process.env.NB_API_KEY;\n  if (!apiKey) {\n    return NextResponse.json({ error: \"NB_API_KEY not configured\" }, { status: 500 });\n  }\n  const q = new URL(request.url).searchParams.get(\"q\")?.trim() ?? \"\";\n  if (q.length < 2) {\n    return NextResponse.json({ suggestions: [] });\n  }\n  const url = new URL(NB_AUTOCOMPLETE_URL);\n  url.searchParams.set(\"q\", q.slice(0, 200));\n  url.searchParams.set(\"at\", LONDON_AT);\n  url.searchParams.set(\"in\", \"countryCode:GBR\");\n  url.searchParams.set(\"limit\", \"6\");\n  url.searchParams.set(\"key\", apiKey);\n\n  const r = await fetch(url, { cache: \"no-store\" });\n  if (!r.ok) {\n    const text = await r.text().catch(() => \"\");\n    return NextResponse.json(\n      { error: `autocomplete failed (${r.status})`, detail: text.slice(0, 500) },\n      { status: 502 },\n    );\n  }\n  const data = (await r.json()) as { items?: NbAutocompleteItem[] };\n  const suggestions: GeocodeSuggestion[] = (data.items ?? [])\n    .filter(\n      (i) =>\n        typeof i.position?.lat === \"number\" && typeof i.position?.lng === \"number\",\n    )\n    .map((i) => ({\n      id: i.id ?? `${i.position!.lat},${i.position!.lng}`,\n      title: i.title ?? i.address?.label ?? \"Unknown\",\n      label: i.address?.label ?? i.title ?? \"Unknown\",\n      lat: i.position!.lat!,\n      lng: i.position!.lng!,\n    }));\n  return NextResponse.json({ suggestions });\n}\n"
}

  - Pins are DOM markers, so they survive the traffic-style swap automatically, and they persist through route Clear/redraw as guides — each is removed via its field's ×.

**Verified**: `npm run build` clean; ran the production build on :3100 and confirmed `/api/geocode?q=tower bridge` returns proper suggestions behind the login gate (test server stopped afterwards).

Not yet built/deployed to Cloud Run or committed — say the word when you want the usual build, deploy, commit and push.

{
 "file_path": "/Users/[USER]/workspace/poc_data/LONDON_COUNCILS/demo/src/app/api/directions/route.ts",
 "content": "import { NextResponse } from \"next/server\";\nimport { decodePolyline, type LngLat } from \"@/lib/geometry\";\n\nconst NB_DIRECTIONS_URL = \"https://api.nextbillion.io/directions/json\";\n\nexport interface DirectionsResponse {\n  /** Route geometry as [lng, lat] pairs. */\n  coordinates: LngLat[];\n  distanceM: number;\n  durationSec: number;\n}\n\nfunction parsePoint(v: string | null): { lat: number; lng: number } | null {\n  if (!v) return null;\n  const m = v.split(\",\");\n  if (m.length !== 2) return null;\n  const lat = Number(m[0]);\n  const lng = Number(m[1]);\n  if (!Number.isFinite(lat) || !Number.isFinite(lng)) return null;\n  if (Math.abs(lat) > 90 || Math.abs(lng) > 180) return null;\n  return { lat, lng };\n}\n\n/**\n * Suggested route between origin and destination via the NextBillion.ai\n * Directions API. GET /api/directions?origin=lat,lng&destination=lat,lng&mode=car|truck\n */\nexport async function GET(request: Request) {\n  const apiKey = process.env.NB_API_KEY;\n  if (!apiKey) {\n    return NextResponse.json({ error: \"NB_API_KEY not configured\" }, { status: 500 });\n  }\n  const params = new URL(request.url).searchParams;\n  const origin = parsePoint(params.get(\"origin\"));\n  const destination = parsePoint(params.get(\"destination\"));\n  if (!origin || !destination) {\n    return NextResponse.json(\n      { error: \"origin and destination required as lat,lng\" },\n      { status: 400 },\n    );\n  }\n  const mode = params.get(\"mode\") === \"truck\" ? \"truck\" : \"car\";\n\n  const url = new URL(NB_DIRECTIONS_URL);\n  url.searchParams.set(\"origin\", `${origin.lat},${origin.lng}`);\n  url.searchParams.set(\"destination\", `${destination.lat},${destination.lng}`);\n  url.searchParams.set(\"mode\", mode);\n  url.searchParams.set(\"geometry\", \"polyline6\");\n  url.searchParams.set(\"key\", apiKey);\n\n  const r = await fetch(url, { cache: \"no-store\" });\n  const data = (await r.json().catch(() => null)) as {\n    status?: string;\n    routes?: Array<{ geometry?: string; distance?: number; duration?: number }>;\n    msg?: string;\n  } | null;\n  const route = data?.routes?.[0];\n  if (!r.ok || data?.status !== \"Ok\" || !route?.geometry) {\n    return NextResponse.json(\n      { error: `directions failed (${data?.status ?? r.status})`, detail: data?.msg ?? \"\" },\n      { status: 502 },\n    );\n  }\n  const body: DirectionsResponse = {\n    coordinates: decodePolyline(route.geometry, 6),\n    distanceM: route.distance ?? 0,\n    durationSec: route.duration ?? 0,\n  };\n  return NextResponse.json(body);\n}\n"
}
```

### CLAUDE (2026-08-19T15:45:44.766Z)

Done. Once both Origin and Destination are set, the app now fetches a route from the NB Directions API and renders it as a light-gray dashed line on the map.

**What was added**
- `src/app/api/directions/route.ts` — proxy to `https://api.nextbillion.io/directions/json` (`GET /api/directions?origin=lat,lng&destination=lat,lng&mode=car|truck`), requests `geometry=polyline6`, decodes server-side and returns `{coordinates, distanceM, durationSec}`. Truck mode adds `option=flexible` — discovered during testing that the default engine returns 422 "no route" for `mode=truck` (this is Directions only; the Navigation API request is unchanged per your earlier instruction).
- `RouteSketcher.tsx`:
  - New `suggested` source + `suggested-line` layer — gray (`#9ca3af`), width 3, dashed `[2,2]` — inserted **below street labels** and **below** the drawn/snapped route, and registered in `APP_SOURCE_IDS`/`UNDER_LABEL_SOURCE_IDS` so it survives the traffic-style swap.
  - Effect: fires whenever both pins are set (and re-fires on pin drag, pin re-search, or Car/Truck profile change), with stale-request aborting; clearing either pin removes the line.
  - Sidebar caption under the search boxes: "⋯ Suggested route: 14.4 km · 54 min".
  - Fixed `fitBounds` padding (left 360px) so the origin pin isn't hidden behind the side panel.

**Verified in the browser** (production build on :3100): Paddington → Canary Wharf shows the dashed line between the green/red pins; switching profile to Truck re-fetched (`/api/directions … mode=truck` → 200, 14.4 km) and redrew; the line and pins persist across the traffic layer toggle. Build is clean; test server and tab cleaned up.

Not yet deployed or committed — say the word for the usual build, deploy, commit and push.

{
 "file_path": "/Users/[USER]/workspace/poc_data/LONDON_COUNCILS/demo/src/lib/route-summary.ts",
 "content": "import type { NavStep } from \"@/app/api/navigate/route\";\nimport { splitRoadRefs } from \"@/lib/shields\";\n\nexport interface RouteSummaryItem {\n  label: string;\n  /** True when the label is a road reference (M/A/B), renderable as a shield. */\n  isRef: boolean;\n}\n\n/**\n * Ordered \"main roads\" summary of a navigation result: one entry per step,\n * using the step's road reference when it has one (M25, A1, ...) and the road\n * or junction name otherwise (Bignell's Corner, ...). Consecutive duplicates\n * are collapsed, so a long run on the A1 appears once until the route leaves\n * it — which reproduces the classic \"B157 / A1000 / M25 / Bignell's Corner /\n * A1 / ...\" permit summary line.\n */\nexport function routeSummary(steps: NavStep[]): RouteSummaryItem[] {\n  const out: RouteSummaryItem[] = [];\n  for (const st of steps) {\n    const refs = splitRoadRefs(st.reference);\n    const name = st.name?.trim();\n    const item: RouteSummaryItem | null = refs.length\n      ? { label: refs[0], isRef: true }\n      : name\n        ? { label: name, isRef: false }\n        : null;\n    if (!item) continue;\n    if (out.length && out[out.length - 1].label === item.label) continue;\n    out.push(item);\n  }\n  return out;\n}\n"
}
```

### CLAUDE (2026-08-19T16:35:58.777Z)

Done — the "Route Summary [Main Roads]" is back, in both the Directions panel and the permit PDF.

**How it works** — new `src/lib/route-summary.ts` walks the navigation steps in order: a step contributes its road ref (M25, A1…) when it has one, otherwise its road/junction name (Bignell's Corner, Copenhagen Street…); consecutive duplicates collapse, so a long run on the A1 shows once until the route leaves and rejoins it. That reproduces your example's pattern exactly.

**Where it appears**
- **Permit PDF** — a bold "Route Summary [Main Roads]:" block right after the summary fields, items joined with " / ", wrapping across lines. Verified by rendering a test permit in Node with steps mimicking your screenshot; the output reads `B157 / A1000 / A111 / M25 / Bignell's Corner / A1 / Stirling Corner / A1 / Mill Hill Circus / A1 / A503 / A5203 / Copenhagen Street / Barnsbury Road` — a match.
- **Directions panel** — a "Route summary (main roads)" strip at the top of the list: mini UK shields for refs, bold text for names, "/" separators. Verified in the browser on a live snapped route (A2213 / Kidbrooke Way / … / A205 / … / A210 chain rendered correctly).

**Bonus fix found while testing**: Generate Permit could hang forever on `map.once("idle")` when the browser throttles rendering (occluded window) — the snapshot wait is now raced against a 4s timeout so the permit always completes.

One note from testing: the NB Navigation API returned "there is no route for input" for a couple of sparse, partially-matched snaps drawn at very low zoom — that's pre-existing upstream behavior unrelated to this change (routes drawn at normal zoom navigate fine).

Build is clean; test server and tabs cleaned up. Not yet deployed or committed — ready for the usual build, deploy, commit and push when you are.

### USER (2026-08-19T16:43:02.367Z)

### CLAUDE (2026-08-19T16:43:25.999Z)

In this context **ERN = Excluded Road Network** — the road network defined by the **London Lorry Control Scheme (LLCS)**, which is operated by London Councils (hence "LCS Routing Tool").

The pieces of the screenshot line up with that reading:

- **The purple roads** on the map are the ERN — the roads *excluded from* the LLCS night-time/weekend restrictions, i.e. the network HGVs over 18 tonnes are supposed to stick to during controlled hours (mostly motorways and A-road corridors).
- **"Compliance Percentage: 84.59%"** is the share of the route that runs on the ERN. Routes 1–3 are ranked by it (84.59% / 57.43% / 81.22%).
- **"Only last mile does not use the ERN"** — the LLCS explicitly allows leaving the ERN for the *shortest practicable route* to the actual origin/destination, since almost no delivery point sits on the network itself. The annotation is pointing out that Route 1 is fully on the ERN except that unavoidable final approach into the destination (the red-boxed area near Camden), which is why it's the preferred/compliant route despite not being 100%.

So the tool is scoring candidate routes by how much of their length stays on the LLCS Excluded Road Network, with off-network mileage only tolerated for first/last-mile access.

Worth noting for our demo: this is an obvious next step for the Route Permit Generator — load the ERN as a network layer (purple overlay), compute a compliance % for the snapped route (length-on-ERN ÷ total length), and flag the off-network segments. The main-roads summary we just added is clearly modelled on this tool's "Route Summary [Main Roads]" line. Happy to build that when you want it.
