### CLAUDE (2026-08-19T16:49:09.177Z)

Good question — the answer depends on whether you want just the purple **look**, or the ERN as **data** (which you'll need anyway if the next step is a compliance %). Three ways, in increasing order of fidelity:

**1. Style-derived overlay (no data, ~1 hour)**
The TomTom vector tiles we already render contain every road classed by type. In `transformBaseStyle` we can clone the line layers for the major classes (`Motorway`, `International road`, `Major road`, toll variants) into new layers painted purple (`#8b5cf6`, ~55% opacity, width ramped by zoom), inserted below labels — same mechanism as our route lines. Result looks exactly like the screenshot instantly.
- Pro: zero data pipeline, always aligned with the basemap.
- Con: it's "all major roads", not the actual ERN (the LLCS network has specific inclusions/exclusions — e.g. some A-roads are *not* excluded roads), and it's purely visual — you can't compute compliance against it.

**2. OSM-derived GeoJSON network (the pragmatic real one)**
Pull `motorway|trunk|primary` ways for the Greater London bounding box from the Overpass API, simplify, save as `public/ern.geojson` (~1–2 MB), then:

```ts
map.addSource("ern", { type: "geojson", data: "/ern.geojson" });
map.addLayer({ id: "ern-line", type: "line", source: "ern",
  paint: { "line-color": "#8b5cf6",
           "line-width": ["interpolate", ["linear"], ["zoom"], 8, 1.5, 14, 6],
           "line-opacity": 0.55 } }, labelsId);
```

registered in `APP_SOURCE_IDS`/`UNDER_LABEL_SOURCE_IDS` so it survives the traffic-style swap, with a toggle button like the traffic control. This is still an approximation of the true ERN, but crucially it's **geometry we own** — the compliance % (route length on ERN ÷ total, with a snap tolerance) falls straight out of it, and we can hand-edit membership per demo feedback.

**3. Official LLCS data**
London Councils' own interactive ERN map (londonlorrycontrol.com) is the authoritative source. If it's backed by an ArcGIS FeatureServer, the layer can usually be exported as GeoJSON via a `f=geojson` query; otherwise the data tends to be available on request / via the London Datastore. Same rendering as option 2 once obtained — this is the "real ERN" path, but it needs me to go find out what's actually downloadable.

**My recommendation:** option 2 — one-time Overpass extraction script checked into `LONDON_COUNCILS/scripts/`, static GeoJSON in `public/`, purple toggle layer. Demo-credible visually *and* it's the foundation for the compliance score, which option 1 can never give you. If you only need the visual for a screenshot tomorrow, option 1 is the fastest.

Want me to build option 2 (I'd also check whether the official data in option 3 is trivially fetchable while I'm at it)?

### CLAUDE (2026-08-19T16:50:18.658Z)

[tool: Write]
```json
{
 "file_path": "/Users/[USER]/workspace/poc_data/LONDON_COUNCILS/scripts/build-ern.mjs",
 "content": "#!/usr/bin/env node\n/**\n * Builds demo/public/ern.geojson — an approximation of the London Lorry\n * Control Scheme \"Excluded Road Network\" (the purple network on the LCS\n * Routing Tool), derived from OpenStreetMap via the Overpass API.\n *\n * The real ERN is roughly the strategic road network in and around Greater\n * London: motorways, trunk roads and primary A-roads (plus their slip\n * roads). This script pulls those classes for a Greater-London bounding box,\n * simplifies the geometry, and writes a compact GeoJSON FeatureCollection.\n *\n * Usage: node LONDON_COUNCILS/scripts/build-ern.mjs\n */\nimport { writeFileSync, mkdirSync } from \"node:fs\";\nimport { dirname, join } from \"node:path\";\nimport { fileURLToPath } from \"node:url\";\n\nconst OVERPASS_URL = \"https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter\";\n// south, west, north, east — Greater London plus the M25 corridor.\nconst BBOX = \"51.20,-0.62,51.78,0.42\";\n// Douglas–Peucker tolerance in degrees (~4–5 m). The overlay is drawn at\n// city zooms, so this is invisible but roughly halves the file size.\nconst SIMPLIFY_DEG = 0.00004;\n\nconst QUERY = `\n[out:json][timeout:180];\nway[\"highway\"~\"^(motorway|trunk|primary|motorway_link|trunk_link|primary_link)$\"](${BBOX});\nout geom tags;\n`;\n\n/** Perpendicular distance from p to segment ab (all [lon, lat]). */\nfunction perpDist(p, a, b) {\n  const dx = b[0] - a[0];\n  const dy = b[1] - a[1];\n  if (dx === 0 && dy === 0) return Math.hypot(p[0] - a[0], p[1] - a[1]);\n  const t = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, ((p[0] - a[0]) * dx + (p[1] - a[1]) * dy) / (dx * dx + dy * dy)));\n  return Math.hypot(p[0] - (a[0] + t * dx), p[1] - (a[1] + t * dy));\n}\n\n/** Iterative Douglas–Peucker. */\nfunction simplify(coords, tol) {\n  if (coords.length <= 2) return coords;\n  const keep = new Array(coords.length).fill(false);\n  keep[0] = keep[coords.length - 1] = true;\n  const stack = [[0, coords.length - 1]];\n  while (stack.length) {\n    const [s, e] = stack.pop();\n    let maxD = 0;\n    let maxI = -1;\n    for (let i = s + 1; i < e; i++) {\n      const d = perpDist(coords[i], coords[s], coords[e]);\n      if (d > maxD) {\n        maxD = d;\n        maxI = i;\n      }\n    }\n    if (maxD > tol) {\n      keep[maxI] = true;\n      stack.push([s, maxI], [maxI, e]);\n    }\n  }\n  return coords.filter((_, i) => keep[i]);\n}\n\nconst round5 = (n) => Math.round(n * 1e5) / 1e5;\n\nasync function main() {\n  console.log(\"Querying Overpass (motorway/trunk/primary + links, Greater London)…\");\n  const r = await fetch(OVERPASS_URL, {\n    method: \"POST\",\n    headers: { \"content-type\": \"application/x-www-form-urlencoded\" },\n    body: `data=${encodeURIComponent(QUERY)}`,\n  });\n  if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`Overpass ${r.status}: ${(await r.text()).slice(0, 300)}`);\n  const data = await r.json();\n  const ways = (data.elements ?? []).filter((e) => e.type === \"way\" && Array.isArray(e.geometry));\n  console.log(`Overpass returned ${ways.length} ways`);\n\n  let ptsIn = 0;\n  let ptsOut = 0;\n  const features = ways.map((w) => {\n    const raw = w.geometry.map((g) => [g.lon, g.lat]);\n    ptsIn += raw.length;\n    const coords = simplify(raw, SIMPLIFY_DEG).map(([x, y]) => [round5(x), round5(y)]);\n    ptsOut += coords.length;\n    const t = w.tags ?? {};\n    const properties = {};\n    if (t.ref) properties.ref = t.ref;\n    if (t.name) properties.name = t.name;\n    properties.class = t.highway;\n    return { type: \"Feature\", properties, geometry: { type: \"LineString\", coordinates: coords } };\n  });\n\n  const fc = { type: \"FeatureCollection\", features };\n  const outPath = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), \"..\", \"demo\", \"public\", \"ern.geojson\");\n  mkdirSync(dirname(outPath), { recursive: true });\n  const json = JSON.stringify(fc);\n  writeFileSync(outPath, json);\n  console.log(\n    `Wrote ${outPath}\\n${features.length} features, ${ptsIn} → ${ptsOut} points, ${(json.length / 1e6).toFixed(1)} MB`,\n  );\n}\n\nmain().catch((e) => {\n  console.error(e);\n  process.exit(1);\n});\n"
}
```

 "new_string": "/** Map button toggling the purple ERN (Excluded Road Network) overlay. */\nclass ErnToggleControl implements maplibregl.IControl {\n  private container: HTMLDivElement | null = null;\n  private button: HTMLButtonElement | null = null;\n  private on = true;\n  constructor(private readonly onToggle: (next: boolean) => void) {}\n  onAdd(): HTMLElement {\n    this.container = document.createElement(\"div\");\n    this.container.className = \"maplibregl-ctrl maplibregl-ctrl-group\";\n    this.button = document.createElement(\"button\");\n    this.button.type = \"button\";\n    this.button.setAttribute(\"aria-label\", \"Toggle ERN overlay\");\n    this.button.style.fontSize = \"9px\";\n    this.button.style.fontWeight = \"700\";\n    this.button.style.color = \"#6d28d9\";\n    this.button.textContent = \"ERN\";\n    this.button.addEventListener(\"click\", () => this.onToggle(!this.on));\n    this.container.appendChild(this.button);\n    this.setActive(this.on);\n    return this.container;\n  }\n  onRemove(): void {\n    this.container?.remove();\n    this.container = null;\n    this.button = null;\n  }\n  setActive(on: boolean): void {\n    this.on = on;\n    if (!this.button) return;\n    this.button.setAttribute(\"aria-pressed\", String(on));\n    this.button.style.background = on ? \"#ede9fe\" : \"\";\n    this.button.title = on\n      ? \"Hide the Excluded Road Network overlay\"\n      : \"Show the Excluded Road Network overlay\";\n  }\n}\n\n// How aggressively the freehand stroke is thinned before it goes to"
}

 "content": "import { Storage } from \"@google-cloud/storage\";\nimport type { SavedRoute } from \"@/lib/saved-routes\";\n\n/**\n * Server-side store for saved routes, shared by all users: one JSON object\n * per route in a GCS bucket (created by terraform, name via ROUTES_BUCKET).\n * Auth is Application Default Credentials — the Cloud Run service account in\n * production, `gcloud auth application-default login` locally.\n */\n\nconst PREFIX = \"routes/\";\nconst MAX_ROUTES = 200;\n\nlet storage: Storage | null = null;\nfunction bucket() {\n  const name = process.env.ROUTES_BUCKET;\n  if (!name) throw new Error(\"ROUTES_BUCKET not configured\");\n  if (!storage) storage = new Storage();\n  return storage.bucket(name);\n}\n\nexport function isConfigured(): boolean {\n  return !!process.env.ROUTES_BUCKET;\n}\n\nfunction isSavedRoute(r: unknown): r is SavedRoute {\n  const x = r as SavedRoute;\n  return (\n    !!x &&\n    typeof x.id === \"string\" &&\n    typeof x.name === \"string\" &&\n    Array.isArray(x.drawnPath) &&\n    !!x.result &&\n    Array.isArray(x.result.coordinates)\n  );\n}\n\nexport async function listRoutes(): Promise<SavedRoute[]> {\n  const [files] = await bucket().getFiles({ prefix: PREFIX, maxResults: MAX_ROUTES });\n  const routes = await Promise.all(\n    files\n      .filter((f) => f.name.endsWith(\".json\"))\n      .map(async (f) => {\n        try {\n          const [buf] = await f.download();\n          const parsed = JSON.parse(buf.toString(\"utf8\"));\n          return isSavedRoute(parsed) ? parsed : null;\n        } catch {\n          return null;\n        }\n      }),\n  );\n  return routes\n    .filter((r): r is SavedRoute => !!r)\n    .sort((a, b) => (a.updatedAt < b.updatedAt ? 1 : -1));\n}\n\nexport async function getRoute(id: string): Promise<SavedRoute | null> {\n  try {\n    const [buf] = await bucket().file(`${PREFIX}${id}.json`).download();\n    const parsed = JSON.parse(buf.toString(\"utf8\"));\n    return isSavedRoute(parsed) ? parsed : null;\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\nexport async function putRoute(route: SavedRoute): Promise<void> {\n  await bucket()\n    .file(`${PREFIX}${route.id}.json`)\n    .save(JSON.stringify(route), {\n      contentType: \"application/json\",\n      resumable: false,\n    });\n}\n\nexport async function deleteRouteObject(id: string): Promise<void> {\n  await bucket()\n    .file(`${PREFIX}${id}.json`)\n    .delete({ ignoreNotFound: true });\n}\n"
}

 "content": "import type { LngLat } from \"@/lib/geometry\";\nimport type { SnapResponse } from \"@/app/api/snap/route\";\n\n/** A named must-pass stop attached to a control vertex. */\nexport interface Waypoint {\n  id: number;\n  label: string;\n}\n/** Editable control vertex of the snapped route. */\nexport interface Vertex {\n  pos: LngLat;\n  wp?: Waypoint;\n}\nexport interface SnapResult extends SnapResponse {\n  drawnLengthM: number;\n  sentPoints: LngLat[];\n}\n\n/** Everything needed to restore a generated route in a later session. */\nexport interface SavedRoute {\n  id: string;\n  name: string;\n  createdAt: string; // ISO\n  updatedAt: string; // ISO\n  mode: \"car\" | \"truck\";\n  radiusM: number;\n  drawnPath: LngLat[];\n  controlPoints: Vertex[] | null;\n  result: SnapResult;\n}\n\n// Phase 2: server storage — routes live in a GCS bucket shared by all users,\n// accessed through /api/routes. (Phase 1 kept them in browser localStorage.)\nconst CHANGE_EVENT = \"london_councils:saved-routes-changed\";\n\nasync function jsonOrThrow<T>(r: Response): Promise<T> {\n  if (!r.ok) {\n    let detail = \"\";\n    try {\n      detail = ((await r.json()) as { error?: string }).error ?? \"\";\n    } catch {\n      /* ignore */\n    }\n    throw new Error(detail || `request failed (${r.status})`);\n  }\n  return (await r.json()) as T;\n}\n\nfunction notifyChanged(): void {\n  if (typeof window !== \"undefined\") window.dispatchEvent(new Event(CHANGE_EVENT));\n}\n\nexport async function listSavedRoutes(): Promise<SavedRoute[]> {\n  const data = await jsonOrThrow<{ routes: SavedRoute[] }>(\n    await fetch(\"/api/routes\", { cache: \"no-store\" }),\n  );\n  return data.routes;\n}\n\nexport function newRouteId(): string {\n  return typeof crypto !== \"undefined\" && \"randomUUID\" in crypto\n    ? crypto.randomUUID()\n    : `${Date.now().toString(36)}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 10)}`;\n}\n\n/** Insert or replace (by id). Returns the stored record. */\nexport async function saveRoute(route: SavedRoute): Promise<SavedRoute> {\n  const data = await jsonOrThrow<{ route: SavedRoute }>(\n    await fetch(`/api/routes/${encodeURIComponent(route.id)}`, {\n      method: \"PUT\",\n      headers: { \"content-type\": \"application/json\" },\n      body: JSON.stringify(route),\n    }),\n  );\n  notifyChanged();\n  return data.route;\n}\n\nexport async function renameRoute(id: string, name: string): Promise<void> {\n  await jsonOrThrow(\n    await fetch(`/api/routes/${encodeURIComponent(id)}`, {\n      method: \"PUT\",\n      headers: { \"content-type\": \"application/json\" },\n      body: JSON.stringify({ name }),\n    }),\n  );\n  notifyChanged();\n}\n\nexport async function deleteRoute(id: string): Promise<void> {\n  await jsonOrThrow(\n    await fetch(`/api/routes/${encodeURIComponent(id)}`, { method: \"DELETE\" }),\n  );\n  notifyChanged();\n}\n\n/** Subscribe to same-tab mutations (server storage has no push channel). */\nexport function onSavedRoutesChange(cb: () => void): () => void {\n  if (typeof window === \"undefined\") return () => {};\n  window.addEventListener(CHANGE_EVENT, cb);\n  return () => window.removeEventListener(CHANGE_EVENT, cb);\n}\n"
}

 "content": "import type { LngLat } from \"@/lib/geometry\";\n\n/**\n * ERN compliance: how much of a route runs on the Excluded Road Network\n * (the purple overlay, /ern.geojson). The route is sampled every ~20 m and\n * each sample is classified by distance to the nearest ERN segment, using a\n * grid index in a local equirectangular projection. Mirrors the LCS Routing\n * Tool's \"Compliance Percentage\".\n */\n\nexport interface ComplianceResult {\n  /** 0–100, length-weighted share of the route on the ERN. */\n  pct: number;\n  onM: number;\n  offM: number;\n  /** Off-network stretches of the route, for rendering ([lng,lat] runs). */\n  offSegments: LngLat[][];\n}\n\n// A route point counts as \"on network\" within this distance of an ERN\n// segment. Covers OSM-vs-TomTom geometry offsets, carriageway separation and\n// the ~5 m simplification applied when building ern.geojson.\nconst TOLERANCE_M = 35;\nconst SAMPLE_M = 20;\nconst CELL_M = 300;\n\n// Local equirectangular projection around London.\nconst LAT0 = 51.5;\nconst M_PER_DEG_LAT = 110_574;\nconst M_PER_DEG_LNG = 111_320 * Math.cos((LAT0 * Math.PI) / 180);\n\ntype XY = [number, number];\nconst toXY = ([lng, lat]: LngLat): XY => [lng * M_PER_DEG_LNG, lat * M_PER_DEG_LAT];\n\ninterface Index {\n  /** cell key -> indices into segs */\n  cells: Map<string, number[]>;\n  /** flat segments [x1, y1, x2, y2, ...] */\n  segs: Float64Array;\n}\n\nfunction cellKey(cx: number, cy: number): string {\n  return `${cx}:${cy}`;\n}\n\nfunction buildIndex(lines: LngLat[][]): Index {\n  const flat: number[] = [];\n  const cells = new Map<string, number[]>();\n  for (const line of lines) {\n    for (let i = 0; i + 1 < line.length; i++) {\n      const [x1, y1] = toXY(line[i]);\n      const [x2, y2] = toXY(line[i + 1]);\n      const idx = flat.length / 4;\n      flat.push(x1, y1, x2, y2);\n      // Register the segment in every cell its bounding box touches.\n      const minCx = Math.floor(Math.min(x1, x2) / CELL_M);\n      const maxCx = Math.floor(Math.max(x1, x2) / CELL_M);\n      const minCy = Math.floor(Math.min(y1, y2) / CELL_M);\n      const maxCy = Math.floor(Math.max(y1, y2) / CELL_M);\n      for (let cx = minCx; cx <= maxCx; cx++) {\n        for (let cy = minCy; cy <= maxCy; cy++) {\n          const k = cellKey(cx, cy);\n          let arr = cells.get(k);\n          if (!arr) cells.set(k, (arr = []));\n          arr.push(idx);\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  return { cells, segs: Float64Array.from(flat) };\n}\n\nfunction distSqToSeg(px: number, py: number, x1: number, y1: number, x2: number, y2: number): number {\n  const dx = x2 - x1;\n  const dy = y2 - y1;\n  const lenSq = dx * dx + dy * dy;\n  let t = lenSq === 0 ? 0 : ((px - x1) * dx + (py - y1) * dy) / lenSq;\n  t = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, t));\n  const ex = px - (x1 + t * dx);\n  const ey = py - (y1 + t * dy);\n  return ex * ex + ey * ey;\n}\n\nfunction nearNetwork(index: Index, p: XY): boolean {\n  const tolSq = TOLERANCE_M * TOLERANCE_M;\n  const cx = Math.floor(p[0] / CELL_M);\n  const cy = Math.floor(p[1] / CELL_M);\n  for (let ix = cx - 1; ix <= cx + 1; ix++) {\n    for (let iy = cy - 1; iy <= cy + 1; iy++) {\n      const arr = index.cells.get(cellKey(ix, iy));\n      if (!arr) continue;\n      for (const s of arr) {\n        const o = s * 4;\n        if (\n          distSqToSeg(p[0], p[1], index.segs[o], index.segs[o + 1], index.segs[o + 2], index.segs[o + 3]) <= tolSq\n        ) {\n          return true;\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  return false;\n}\n\nlet indexPromise: Promise<Index> | null = null;\nfunction loadIndex(): Promise<Index> {\n  if (!indexPromise) {\n    indexPromise = fetch(\"/ern.geojson\")\n      .then((r) => {\n        if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`ern.geojson ${r.status}`);\n        return r.json() as Promise<GeoJSON.FeatureCollection>;\n      })\n      .then((fc) => {\n        const lines: LngLat[][] = [];\n        for (const f of fc.features) {\n          if (f.geometry.type === \"MultiLineString\") {\n            lines.push(...(f.geometry.coordinates as LngLat[][]));\n          } else if (f.geometry.type === \"LineString\") {\n            lines.push(f.geometry.coordinates as LngLat[]);\n          }\n        }\n        return buildIndex(lines);\n      })\n      .catch((e) => {\n        indexPromise = null; // allow a retry on the next call\n        throw e;\n      });\n  }\n  return indexPromise;\n}\n\n/**\n * Classify a route polyline against the ERN. Samples every ~20 m; consecutive\n * off-network samples are merged into `offSegments` for rendering.\n */\nexport async function computeCompliance(coords: LngLat[]): Promise<ComplianceResult | null> {\n  if (coords.length < 2) return null;\n  const index = await loadIndex();\n  let onM = 0;\n  let offM = 0;\n  const offSegments: LngLat[][] = [];\n  let currentOff: LngLat[] | null = null;\n\n  const endOff = () => {\n    if (currentOff && currentOff.length >= 2) offSegments.push(currentOff);\n    currentOff = null;\n  };\n\n  for (let i = 0; i + 1 < coords.length; i++) {\n    const a = coords[i];\n    const b = coords[i + 1];\n    const [ax, ay] = toXY(a);\n    const [bx, by] = toXY(b);\n    const segLen = Math.hypot(bx - ax, by - ay);\n    if (segLen === 0) continue;\n    const steps = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(segLen / SAMPLE_M));\n    for (let s = 0; s < steps; s++) {\n      const t0 = s / steps;\n      const t1 = (s + 1) / steps;\n      const tm = (t0 + t1) / 2;\n      const mid: XY = [ax + (bx - ax) * tm, ay + (by - ay) * tm];\n      const p0: LngLat = [a[0] + (b[0] - a[0]) * t0, a[1] + (b[1] - a[1]) * t0];\n      const p1: LngLat = [a[0] + (b[0] - a[0]) * t1, a[1] + (b[1] - a[1]) * t1];\n      const stepLen = segLen / steps;\n      if (nearNetwork(index, mid)) {\n        onM += stepLen;\n        endOff();\n      } else {\n        offM += stepLen;\n        if (!currentOff) currentOff = [p0];\n        currentOff.push(p1);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  endOff();\n  const total = onM + offM;\n  return {\n    pct: total > 0 ? (onM / total) * 100 : 0,\n    onM,\n    offM,\n    offSegments,\n  };\n}\n"
}

// Route A: along the A2 Blackheath->Dartford corridor (on-network expected).
// Use NB directions car route Westminster->Tower Bridge (mostly A-roads).

EOF

### CLAUDE (2026-08-19T18:14:21.025Z)

Good eye — ours is denser for three reasons, and the client's use case actually tells us which filters are right.

**Why our layer is denser than the client's**

1. **We took *every* `primary` A-road** (plus all slip-road `*_link`s). The real LLCS ERN is a *curated* subset of principal roads — roughly "motorways + trunk + the more strategic A-roads". Look at the client image: the M25/A1(M)/A10/A406/A2-class roads are purple, but most **4-digit A-roads** (A1000, A5203, A1081…) are *not* — that's why their own route summary (A1000, A5203, Copenhagen Street) scores only 84.59% compliant.
2. **OSM dual carriageways are two parallel ways**, so big roads render double-stroked at our 50% opacity, reading as extra density.
3. **We render the same density everywhere in the bbox**, while their portal only cares about the network **inside the M25**.

**Filters I'd apply, mapped to the use case**

1. **Clip the ERN to the M25 orbital (keeping the M25 itself)** — the spec says it outright: *outside the M25 it's a regular truck route; inside it's the council-approved network*. So the overlay and the compliance denominator should only cover the inside-M25 portion of a route; the Harlow leg outside the orbital shouldn't count against compliance at all. This is the biggest correctness *and* density win.
2. **Ref-digit pruning**: keep `M*`, `A*(M)`, and A-roads with **1–3 digit refs** (A1, A10, A406); drop 4-digit A-roads (A1000, A5203…). In UK numbering fewer digits ≈ more strategic, and it matches the client image well. (Requires keeping `ref` per feature in `build-ern.mjs` — we currently discard it.)
3. **Drop `*_link` slip roads from the *display*** but keep them in the compliance index (so a compliant route isn't penalised at junctions).
4. Cosmetic: slightly lower opacity / raise minzoom for `primary` so remaining density reads like their map.

**The honest caveat**: any OSM heuristic is an approximation. The authoritative fix is to get the actual **LLCS ERN dataset from London Councils / the client** (they clearly have it — their portal renders it). Our architecture makes the swap trivial: replace `public/ern.geojson` and both the overlay and the compliance score update, no code change.

Also worth mirroring their UX: compliance would then read "100% of the in-M25 portion on approved network, 1.2 km last-mile off-network", which is exactly the "only last mile does not use the ERN" framing in their screenshot.

Want me to implement 1–3? The M25 clip is the only non-trivial piece (I'd assemble the M25 ways into a ring from the same Overpass pull and clip/classify against that polygon, both in the build script and in the compliance calc).

### CLAUDE (2026-08-20T12:26:40.823Z)

### CLAUDE (2026-08-20T12:26:43.039Z)

[tool: Edit]
```json
{
 "replace_all": false,
 "file_path": "/Users/[USER]/workspace/poc_data/LONDON_COUNCILS/demo/src/app/globals.css",
 "old_string": "/* Make room for the Sign out button in the top-right corner. */\n.maplibregl-ctrl-top-right {\n  top: 2.4rem;\n}",
 "new_string": "/* Make room for the Sign out button in the top-right corner. maplibre's own\n   stylesheet (imported later in the bundle) sets top: 0, so this needs\n   !important to win. */\n.maplibregl-ctrl-top-right {\n  top: 2.6rem !important;\n}"
}
```

### CLAUDE (2026-08-20T12:26:48.211Z)

[tool: Bash — Build after CSS fix]
```bash

```

### CLAUDE (2026-08-20T12:27:01.898Z)

Fixed — the earlier `top: 2.4rem` rule was being overridden by MapLibre's own stylesheet (it loads after `globals.css` in the bundle and resets `top: 0`), so the traffic button was sitting hidden behind the Sign out button. The rule now carries `!important` and a slightly larger offset (`2.6rem`), so the stack reads: **Sign out → 🚦 traffic → ERN**, no overlap.

Build clean; refresh the :3101 tab to see it. Still pending deploy: Sign out relocation, zoom-control removal, and this fix — say the word.

### CLAUDE (2026-08-20T13:18:00.359Z)

Writing the shared hook into each app and wiring it up:

### CLAUDE (2026-08-20T13:18:05.309Z)

[tool: Bash — Create useStoredKey hook in both apps]
```bash
for APP in GEOCODE_DEMO AUTO_CARRIER; do cat > $APP/demo/src/lib/use-stored-key.ts <<'EOF'
"use client";

import { useEffect, useState } from "react";

/**
 * useState persisted to localStorage, so a key the user pastes survives page
 * reloads. Falls back to `fallback` (e.g. a NEXT_PUBLIC env value) when
 * nothing is stored; clearing the field removes the stored value.
 */
export function useStoredKey(
  storageKey: string,
  fallback: string,
): [string, (v: string) => void] {
  const [value, setValue] = useState(fallback);
  useEffect(() => {
    try {
      const stored = window.localStorage.getItem(storageKey);
      if (stored) setValue(stored);
    } catch {
      // Storage unavailable (private mode etc.) — keep the fallback.
    }
  }, [storageKey]);
  const set = (v: string) => {
    setValue(v);
    try {
      if (v) window.localStorage.setItem(storageKey, v);
      else window.localStorage.removeItem(storageKey);
    } catch {
      // Ignore quota/availability errors; the in-memory value still works.
    }
  };
  return [value, set];
}
EOF
done; ls GEOCODE_DEMO/demo/src/lib/use-stored-key.ts AUTO_CARRIER/demo/src/lib/use-stored-key.ts
```

Done — pasted API keys now persist in the browser's localStorage and are restored on page load, in both demos that have key fields:

- **GEOCODE_DEMO** — both keys persist: NB key (`geocode_demo.nb_api_key`) and Google Maps fallback key (`geocode_demo.gmaps_api_key`).
- **AUTO_CARRIER** — the NB key persists (`auto_carrier.nb_api_key`).

Mechanics (shared `use-stored-key.ts` hook added to each app): on mount, a stored value wins; otherwise the `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` env value is the fallback (so the baked key in the deployed AUTO_CARRIER image still auto-fills). Clearing the field deletes the stored value; private-mode/storage errors are silently tolerated (the in-memory value still works).

One caveat worth stating: localStorage is readable by any script on the page — acceptable for these demos since the same keys are already public in the client bundle/requests, but not a pattern for privileged keys.

 "content": "# Multi-stage Dockerfile for the GEOCODE_DEMO (Forward Geocoding & Search) demo.\n# Build context: the GEOCODE_DEMO/ directory (contains demo/).\n#\n# The browser calls the NB.ai search APIs directly, so the public key is baked\n# into the client bundle at BUILD time via NEXT_PUBLIC_NB_API_KEY:\n#   docker build --platform=linux/amd64 \\\n#     --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_NB_API_KEY=\"$NB_KEY\" -t IMAGE . && docker push IMAGE\n\nFROM node:20-alpine AS deps\nWORKDIR /app\nCOPY demo/package.json demo/package-lock.json* ./\nRUN npm ci\n\nFROM node:20-alpine AS builder\nWORKDIR /app\nARG NEXT_PUBLIC_NB_API_KEY=\"\"\nARG NEXT_PUBLIC_GMAPS_API_KEY=\"\"\nENV NEXT_PUBLIC_NB_API_KEY=${NEXT_PUBLIC_NB_API_KEY}\nENV NEXT_PUBLIC_GMAPS_API_KEY=${NEXT_PUBLIC_GMAPS_API_KEY}\nENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1\nCOPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules\nCOPY demo/ ./\nRUN npm run build\n\nFROM node:20-alpine AS runner\nWORKDIR /app\nENV NODE_ENV=production\nENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1\nENV HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0\n# Cloud Run sets PORT itself; default for local docker-run.\nENV PORT=8080\n\nRUN addgroup -S app && adduser -S app -G app\n\n# Standalone Next.js server.js + minimal node_modules.\nCOPY --from=builder --chown=app:app /app/.next/standalone ./\nCOPY --from=builder --chown=app:app /app/.next/static ./.next/static\nCOPY --from=builder --chown=app:app /app/public ./public\n\nUSER app\nEXPOSE 8080\nCMD [\"node\", \"server.js\"]\n"
}

Fallback items come back with Google place ids (\"ChIJ…\"), which\n  // is how we tag them in the UI.\n  const fallback = panel.gmapsFallback ? \"&fallback=true&score=0.6\" : \"\";\n  const url = `${NB_H}/discover?q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}&limit=${panel.resultLimit}&in=countryCode:${countryList(panel)}&lang=${panel.language}&at=${panel.city.centroid}${fallback}&key=${encodeURIComponent(apiKey)}`;\n  const data = await getJson(url);\n  return (data.items ?? []).map((i) => {\n    const isGoogle = typeof i.id === \"string\" && i.id.startsWith(\"ChIJ\");\n    const f = itemToFeature(i, isGoogle ? \"google\" : \"nbai\");\n    return !isGoogle && (f.scoring ?? 0) < 0.75 ? { ...f, source: \"nbai-low\" as const } : f;\n  });\n}"

            setDetail(await nbLookup(item.id, apiKey, { legacy: !mode.endpoint }));
            setMode({});
          }
        }}
        onClear={() => {
          setDetail(null);
          setMode({});
        }}
      />
      {mode.ontology && (
        <div className="text-[9pt] text-gray-500">
          Category follow-up active: <code>{mode.ontology}</code> (via /orbis/discover)
        </div>
      )}
      <DetailCard title="Selected result — lookup?id=… " data={detail} />'''
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

Done — GEOCODE_DEMO now calls `/orbis` for Discover, Autocomplete, Geocode and Lookup. Local build passes and I verified every example end-to-end in the browser (network requests confirmed hitting `https://api.nextbillion.io/orbis/…`). Changes are local only — not yet built/deployed/committed.

**What the switch required beyond the one-line base change** (all found by probing the live API):

| Difference on `/orbis` | Fix |
|---|---|
| `lang=en` rejected (`unsupported language code`) — wants region tags (`en-US`, `fr-FR`, …; oddly bare `ar`) | `LANGUAGES` list in `data.ts` rewritten to accepted tags; default panel → `en-US`. **Dropped Japanese, Esperanto, Burmese, Yoruba** — orbis rejects them in every form. Added Chinese Traditional (`zh-TW`). |
| **No `/orbis/autosuggest`** (404 — public docs also only list it at root/`/h`) | Example 3 stays on `/h/autosuggest` (`NB_LEGACY` const); page text notes this. Category follow-up now runs on `/orbis/discover` (accepts `_ontology`). |
| Ids aren't interchangeable — `/orbis/lookup` returns empty for `/h` ids | `nbLookup(id, key, {legacy})`; Autosuggest picks resolve via `/h/lookup`, Autocomplete picks via `/orbis/lookup`. Both verified. |
| Score is top-level `score` (not `scoring.queryScore`); scale isn't 0–1 (e.g. "starbucks" = 4.4, weak matches ≈ 0.5–0.6) | `itemToFeature` reads either; "low score" tag still `< 0.75` (in line with the `score=0.6` fallback threshold). |
| `address.label` no longer embeds the POI name; no `type` field; no `highlights` | `placeName` = `"Title, label"` when title isn't in label (Discover table shows "Starbucks, 505 North Grand Avenue…" again); highlight rendering already had a client-side token fallback. |

**Bonus fix:** marker number labels on the maps were silently failing — `Open Sans Bold` glyphs 404 against the `basic_main` style (left over from last session's style switch). Switched `text-font` to `Noto-Bold`; the 1–5 labels render now.

### CLAUDE (2026-08-23T15:27:57.279Z)

[tool: Bash — Enable building extrusion layers at high zoom in ResultsMap]
```bash
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='src/components/ResultsMap.tsx'; s=open(p).read()
old='''        mapRef.current = nbmap;
        nbmap.map.on("load", () => {
          readyRef.current = true;
          sync();
        });'''
new='''        mapRef.current = nbmap;
        nbmap.map.on("load", () => {
          readyRef.current = true;
          enableBuildings(nbmap.map);
          sync();
        });'''
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new)
old='''interface Props {'''
new='''// Zoom from which building footprints/extrusions are shown.
const BUILDINGS_MIN_ZOOM = 15.5;

// The basic_main style ships building footprints as flat fills (visible from
// z12, very faint) plus "* building 3D" fill-extrusion layers that are hidden
// by default. Turn the extrusion layers on when zoomed far in: at the default
// flat pitch they render as clearly shaded footprints, and become 3D when the
// user tilts the map (right-drag / ctrl-drag).
function enableBuildings(map: any) {
  const style = map.getStyle();
  if (!style?.layers) return;
  for (const layer of style.layers) {
    if (layer.type !== "fill-extrusion" || !/building/i.test(layer.id)) continue;
    map.setLayoutProperty(layer.id, "visibility", "visible");
    map.setLayerZoomRange(layer.id, BUILDINGS_MIN_ZOOM, 24);
    map.setPaintProperty(layer.id, "fill-extrusion-opacity", 0.85);
    // Buildings without a height still show as a low footprint slab.
    map.setPaintProperty(layer.id, "fill-extrusion-height", [
      "coalesce",
      ["get", "height"],
      3,
    ]);
    map.setPaintProperty(layer.id, "fill-extrusion-base", [
      "coalesce",
      ["get", "ground_height"],
      0,
    ]);
    map.setFilter(layer.id, null);
  }
}

interface Props {'''
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new,1)
# allow fitBounds/ selection to zoom in far enough to see buildings when a single result is selected
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
grep -n "maxZoom" src/components/ResultsMap.tsx
```

### CLAUDE (2026-08-23T15:29:58.946Z)

[tool: Bash — Replace extrusions with emphasised 2D footprints; rebuild and restart]
```bash
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='src/components/ResultsMap.tsx'; s=open(p).read()
start=s.index('// Zoom from which building footprints/extrusions are shown.')
end=s.index('interface Props {')
new='''// Zoom from which building footprints are emphasised.
const BUILDINGS_MIN_ZOOM = 15.5;

// The basic_main style ships building footprints as flat fill layers
// ("Other building", "School building", …) that are visible from z12 but very
// faint. (It also has "* building 3D" fill-extrusion layers, hidden by
// default — left off: real heights make downtown towers swamp the map.)
// Past BUILDINGS_MIN_ZOOM, darken the fills and give them a crisp outline so
// the footprints read clearly when zoomed far in.
function emphasiseBuildingFootprints(map: any) {
  const style = map.getStyle();
  if (!style?.layers) return;
  for (const layer of style.layers) {
    if (layer.type !== "fill" || !/building/i.test(layer.id)) continue;
    const isShadow = /shadow/i.test(layer.id);
    const base = layer.paint?.["fill-color"] ?? "rgba(223, 228, 232, 1)";
    const baseOutline = layer.paint?.["fill-outline-color"] ?? base;
    map.setPaintProperty(layer.id, "fill-color", [
      "interpolate",
      ["linear"],
      ["zoom"],
      BUILDINGS_MIN_ZOOM,
      base,
      BUILDINGS_MIN_ZOOM + 1,
      isShadow ? "rgba(160, 165, 172, 1)" : "rgba(196, 203, 210, 1)",
    ]);
    map.setPaintProperty(layer.id, "fill-outline-color", [
      "interpolate",
      ["linear"],
      ["zoom"],
      BUILDINGS_MIN_ZOOM,
      baseOutline,
      BUILDINGS_MIN_ZOOM + 1,
      "rgba(120, 126, 134, 1)",
    ]);
  }
}

'''
s=s[:start]+new+s[end:]
s=s.replace('enableBuildings(nbmap.map);','emphasiseBuildingFootprints(nbmap.map);')
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
npx tsc --noEmit -p . && npm run build 2>&1 | grep -E "error|✓ Compiled" ; pkill -f "next start -p 3201"; sleep 1; (nohup npx next start -p 3201 > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-[USER]-workspace-poc-data/4d4d6596-b0f7-4041-bf4f-cd296037b2f4/scratchpad/geocode-start.log 2>&1 &); sleep 4; curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://localhost:3201/login

### CLAUDE (2026-08-23T15:31:09.650Z)

Yes — and it's now wired up (local only, not yet deployed/committed).

**What the `basic_main` style contains**
- **2D building footprints** — five `fill` layers (`Other building`, `School building`, `Factory building`, `Hospital building`, `Hotel building`, each with a 2px drop-shadow twin), visible from zoom 12 but in very pale gray/tan, so they barely register.
- **3D buildings** — matching `* building 3D` `fill-extrusion` layers driven by `height`/`ground_height` in the tiles, shipped with `visibility: none`.

**What I did** (`GEOCODE_DEMO/demo/src/components/ResultsMap.tsx`)
- On map load, `emphasiseBuildingFootprints()` walks the style and, for every building `fill` layer, interpolates `fill-color`/`fill-outline-color` by zoom: original colors at ≤15.5 → darker gray fill with a crisp outline by 16.5. Below that threshold nothing changes. Verified at z17 in downtown LA — footprints are clearly readable; at z15 it looks as before.
- I first tried enabling the 3D extrusion layers instead, but with real heights the downtown towers render as enormous perspective slabs at z17 and swamp the map — so I left 3D off. If you'd like a tilted-3D option it's a small change (enable those layers + set a pitch), just say so.

Note the result maps `fitBounds` to `maxZoom: 15`, so footprints emphasise only once the user zooms in (double-click/scroll) — matching "when zoomed far in". Ready to build/deploy/commit/push on your word.

### CLAUDE (2026-08-24T13:28:00.778Z)

[tool: Bash — Hide POI layers at z<=15, rebuild, restart server]
```bash
cd /Users/[USER]/workspace/poc_data/GEOCODE_DEMO/demo && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='src/components/ResultsMap.tsx'; s=open(p).read()
old='''// Zoom used when the user selects a single result (far enough in to see its
// building footprint and access point).

new='''// Zoom used when the user selects a single result (far enough in to see its
// building footprint and access point).
const SELECTED_ZOOM = 17;
// POI icons/labels are hidden at zoom <= POI_MIN_ZOOM to keep the overview
// maps clean — search-result markers are the focus there.
const POI_MIN_ZOOM = 15;

// Restrict the style's POI symbol layers (source-layer "poi") so they only
// appear when zoomed in past POI_MIN_ZOOM.
function limitPoiZoom(map: any) {
  const style = map.getStyle();
  if (!style?.layers) return;
  for (const layer of style.layers) {
    if (layer.type !== "symbol" || layer["source-layer"] !== "poi") continue;
    const minzoom = Math.max(layer.minzoom ?? 0, POI_MIN_ZOOM + 0.1);
    map.setLayerZoomRange(layer.id, minzoom, layer.maxzoom ?? 24);
  }
}'''
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new)
old='''          enableBuildings(nbmap.map);'''
# earlier renamed
old2='''          emphasiseBuildingFootprints(nbmap.map);
          sync();'''
new2='''          emphasiseBuildingFootprints(nbmap.map);
          limitPoiZoom(nbmap.map);
          sync();'''
assert old2 in s; s=s.replace(old2,new2)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

old='''export async function nbGeocode(

): Promise<SearchFeature[]> {

new='''// Forward geocode. Request shape:
//   /orbis/geocode?in=countryCode:<list>&q=<query>&at=<lat>,<lng>&key=<key>
// The `at` parameter is required by the endpoint (bias point = selected city).
export async function nbGeocode(
  query: string,
  panel: PanelState,

new='''// Structured geocode: address parts as individual query parameters.
// Request shape (fields per the NB Structured Geocode docs; countryCode is
// required, the rest optional):
//   /orbis/geocode/structured?countryCode=USA&state=…&county=…&city=…
//     &street=…&houseNumber=…&postalCode=…&limit=…&key=<key>
export interface StructuredQuery {
  countryCode: string;
  state?: string;
  county?: string;
  city?: string;
  street?: string;
  houseNumber?: string;
  postalCode?: string;
}

export async function nbStructuredGeocode(
  q: StructuredQuery,
  panel: PanelState,
  apiKey: string
): Promise<SearchFeature[]> {
  const params = new URLSearchParams();
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(q)) {
    if (v && String(v).trim()) params.set(k, String(v).trim());
  }
  params.set("limit", String(panel.resultLimit));
  params.set("key", apiKey);
  const data = await getJson(`${NB_H}/geocode/structured?${params.toString()}`);
  return (data.items ?? []).map((i) => itemToFeature(i));
}

// Reverse geocode: nearest address to the given "lat,lng" point.'''

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Example 6 — Structured Geocode (address parts as individual fields)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

const STRUCTURED_FIELDS: {
  key: keyof StructuredQuery;
  label: string;
  placeholder: string;
  required?: boolean;
}[] = [
  { key: "countryCode", label: "Country Code", placeholder: "USA", required: true },
  { key: "state", label: "State", placeholder: "Ohio" },
  { key: "county", label: "County", placeholder: "Franklin" },
  { key: "city", label: "City", placeholder: "Dublin" },
  { key: "street", label: "Street", placeholder: "Coventry Woods Drive North" },
  { key: "houseNumber", label: "House Number", placeholder: "7592" },
  { key: "postalCode", label: "Postal Code", placeholder: "43017" },
];

export function StructuredGeocodeExample({ panel, apiKey }: ExampleProps) {
  const [query, setQuery] = useState<StructuredQuery>({ countryCode: "USA" });
  const [features, setFeatures] = useState<SearchFeature[]>([]);
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<SearchFeature | null>(null);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);
  const [error, setError] = useState("");

  const canSearch =
    Boolean(query.countryCode?.trim()) &&
    STRUCTURED_FIELDS.some((f) => !f.required && String(query[f.key] ?? "").trim());

  async function run() {
    if (!canSearch || loading) return;
    setLoading(true);
    setError("");
    try {
      const results = await nbStructuredGeocode(query, panel, apiKey);
      setFeatures(results);
      setSelected(null);
    } catch (e) {
      setError(String((e as Error)?.message ?? e));
      setFeatures([]);
      setSelected(null);
    } finally {
      setLoading(false);
    }
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
      <div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-3 sm:grid-cols-4">
        {STRUCTURED_FIELDS.map((f) => (
          <label key={f.key} className="flex flex-col gap-1 text-[9pt] text-gray-600">
            <span>
              {f.label}
              {f.required && <span className="text-red-600"> *</span>}
            </span>
            <input
              className="rounded border border-gray-300 px-2 py-1 text-sm"
              placeholder={f.placeholder}
              value={query[f.key] ?? ""}
              onChange={(e) => setQuery((p) => ({ ...p, [f.key]: e.target.value }))}
              onKeyDown={(e) => {
                if (e.key === "Enter") run();
              }}
            />
          </label>
        ))}
        <div className="flex items-end">
          <button
            type="button"
            className="rounded bg-blue-600 px-4 py-1.5 text-sm font-medium text-white disabled:opacity-50"
            disabled={!canSearch || loading}
            onClick={run}
          >
            {loading ? "Searching…" : "Search"}
          </button>
        </div>
      </div>
      {error && <div className="text-sm text-red-600">{error}</div>}
      <ResultsTable features={features} selected={selected} onSelect={setSelected} />
      <ResultsMap
        apiKey={apiKey}
        center={cityCenter(panel)}
        features={features}
        selected={selected}
        sourceId="structured-results"
      />
    </div>
  );
}'''

### CLAUDE (2026-08-25T12:11:03.862Z)

**No — there's no orbis batch geocode endpoint.** Probed against the live API with the demo key:

| Path | Result |
|---|---|
| `POST /orbis/geocode/batch` | **404** (path not routed) |
| `POST /orbis/batch`, `/orbis/revgeocode/batch`, `/orbis/geocode/structured/batch` | 404 |
| `POST /orbis/geocode` (array body) | 405 — the orbis geocode is GET-only |
| `POST /geocode/batch` | **200** ✓ |
| `POST /h/geocode/batch` | **200** ✓ (same result) |

So batch geocoding is only available on the legacy base: `POST https://api.nextbillion.io/geocode/batch?key=…` with a JSON array of `{q, at, in…}` queries — and it returns the legacy item shape (`type` field, POI-inclusive `address.label`, `/h`-world ids that won't resolve on `/orbis/lookup`).

If you want a batch example in the demo, the options are that legacy endpoint as-is, or fanning out N parallel GETs to `/orbis/geocode` client-side to stay on orbis data. Just say which if you'd like it added.

// legacy batch API: POST /geocode/batch?key=… with a JSON array of forward
// geocode queries; the response is an array of {items:[…]} aligned with the
// request order.
export interface BatchGeocodeQuery {
  q: string;
  at?: string; // "lat,lng" bias
  in?: string; // e.g. "countryCode:USA"
}

export async function nbBatchGeocode(
  queries: BatchGeocodeQuery[],
  apiKey: string
): Promise<SearchFeature[][]> {
  const url = `https://api.nextbillion.io/geocode/batch?key=${encodeURIComponent(apiKey)}`;
  const r = await fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify(queries),
  });
  if (!r.ok) {
    const text = await r.text();
    throw new Error(`HTTP ${r.status}: ${text.slice(0, 200)}`);
  }
  const data: { items?: NbItem[] }[] = await r.json();
  return data.map((entry) => (entry.items ?? []).map((i) => itemToFeature(i)));
}

// Fetch the full record for a previously returned result id.'''

const BATCH_MAX = 50;

function randomBatchQueries(count: number): BatchGeocodeQuery[] {
  const out: BatchGeocodeQuery[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    const c = BATCH_CITIES[Math.floor(Math.random() * BATCH_CITIES.length)];
    const street = BATCH_STREETS[Math.floor(Math.random() * BATCH_STREETS.length)];

export function BatchGeocodeExample({ apiKey }: ExampleProps) {

  const [rows, setRows] = useState<

  >([]);

  const [elapsedMs, setElapsedMs] = useState<number | null>(null);
  const [error, setError] = useState("");

    const n = Math.min(Math.max(1, Math.floor(count) || 1), BATCH_MAX);

    const started = performance.now();
    try {
      const results = await nbBatchGeocode(queries, apiKey);
      setElapsedMs(performance.now() - started);
      setRows(
        queries.map((q, i) => ({ query: q.q, result: results[i]?.[0] ?? null }))
      );
    } catch (e) {
      setError(String((e as Error)?.message ?? e));
      setRows([]);
    } finally {
      setLoading(false);
    }
  }

  return (

      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-end gap-3">

            type="number"
            min={1}
            max={BATCH_MAX}
            className="w-40 rounded border border-gray-300 px-2 py-1 text-sm"
            value={count}
            onChange={(e) => setCount(Number(e.target.value))}
            onKeyDown={(e) => {
              if (e.key === "Enter") run();
            }}
          />
        </label>
        <button
          type="button"
          className="rounded bg-blue-600 px-4 py-1.5 text-sm font-medium text-white disabled:opacity-50"
          disabled={loading}
          onClick={run}

          {loading ? "Geocoding…" : "Batch Geocode"}
        </button>

            {rows.length} queries in {(elapsedMs / 1000).toFixed(2)}s
          </span>
        )}
      </div>
      {error && <div className="text-sm text-red-600">{error}</div>}
      {rows.length > 0 && (

                  <td>{fmtLatLng(row.result?.center)}</td>
                </tr>
              ))}
            </tbody>
          </table>

}'''

# ---------------- nb.ts ----------------
p='src/lib/nb.ts'; s=open(p).read()
old='''// Batch geocode.'''
new='''// Postal code lookup. There is no /orbis equivalent — this is the standard
// Geocode Postcode API: POST /postalcode?key=… with a JSON body of
// {postalcode, country, at?}. `country` is required with `postalcode`; `at`
// ({lat,lng}) biases the lookup. The response's places[] carry a geopoint and
// a boundary as {multiPolygon:[{polygon:[{points:[{lat,lng}…]}…]}…]}, which is
// converted here to a GeoJSON MultiPolygon for rendering.
export interface PostalCodeResult {
  feature: SearchFeature;
  boundary: GeoJSON.Feature | null;
}

export async function nbPostalCode(
  body: { postalcode: string; country: string; at?: { lat: number; lng: number } },
  apiKey: string
): Promise<PostalCodeResult[]> {
  const url = `https://api.nextbillion.io/postalcode?key=${encodeURIComponent(apiKey)}`;
  const r = await fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  });
  if (!r.ok) {
    const text = await r.text();
    throw new Error(`HTTP ${r.status}: ${text.slice(0, 200)}`);
  }
  const data = await r.json();
  type Pt = { lat: number; lng: number };
  type Place = {
    geopoint?: Pt;
    address?: string;
    postalCode?: string;
    boundary?: { multiPolygon?: { polygon?: { points?: Pt[] }[] }[] };
    [k: string]: unknown;
  };
  return ((data.places ?? []) as Place[]).map((place) => {
    const coords: number[][][][] = (place.boundary?.multiPolygon ?? []).map((mp) =>
      (mp.polygon ?? []).map((ring) =>
        (ring.points ?? []).map((pt) => [pt.lng, pt.lat])
      )
    );
    const boundary: GeoJSON.Feature | null = coords.length
      ? {
          type: "Feature",
          properties: { postalCode: place.postalCode ?? "" },
          geometry: { type: "MultiPolygon", coordinates: coords },
        }
      : null;
    const feature: SearchFeature = {
      id: undefined,
      placeName: place.address ?? place.postalCode ?? "",
      resultType: "postalCode",
      placeType: "Postal Code",
      scoring: undefined,
      center: place.geopoint ? [place.geopoint.lng, place.geopoint.lat] : undefined,
      access: undefined,
      source: "nbai",
      fullResult: place as Record<string, unknown>,
    };
    return { feature, boundary };
  });
}

// Batch geocode.'''

new='''export function StructuredGeocodeExample({ panel, apiKey }: ExampleProps) {
  const [query, setQuery] = useState<StructuredQuery>({ countryCode: "USA" });
  const [features, setFeatures] = useState<SearchFeature[]>([]);
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<SearchFeature | null>(null);
  const [boundary, setBoundary] = useState<GeoJSON.Feature | null>(null);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);
  const [error, setError] = useState("");
  const viewRef = useRef<MapViewHandle | null>(null);

  const canSearch =
    Boolean(query.countryCode?.trim()) &&
    STRUCTURED_FIELDS.some((f) => !f.required && String(query[f.key] ?? "").trim());

  // With only a postal code (plus the required country code) filled in, the
  // dedicated Postcode API is used instead of structured geocoding — it also
  // returns the postal code's boundary polygon for the map.
  const postalOnly =
    Boolean(query.postalCode?.trim()) &&
    STRUCTURED_FIELDS.every(
      (f) =>
        f.required ||
        f.key === "postalCode" ||
        !String(query[f.key] ?? "").trim()
    );

  async function run() {
    if (!canSearch || loading) return;
    setLoading(true);
    setError("");
    try {
      if (postalOnly) {
        // `at` = centroid of the currently displayed map view.
        const [lat, lng] = viewRef.current?.getCenter() ?? cityCenter(panel);
        const places = await nbPostalCode(
          {
            postalcode: query.postalCode!.trim(),
            country: query.countryCode.trim(),
            at: { lat, lng },
          },
          apiKey
        );
        setFeatures(places.map((p) => p.feature));
        setBoundary(places[0]?.boundary ?? null);
      } else {
        const results = await nbStructuredGeocode(query, panel, apiKey);
        setFeatures(results);
        setBoundary(null);
      }
      setSelected(null);
    } catch (e) {
      setError(String((e as Error)?.message ?? e));
      setFeatures([]);
      setBoundary(null);
      setSelected(null);
    } finally {
      setLoading(false);
    }
  }'''

### CLAUDE (2026-08-25T12:39:03.852Z)

Done locally — with **one deliberate deviation you should know about**.

**What's implemented**
- In Example 5 (Structured Geocode), when only Country Code + Postal Code are filled, the button relabels to **Postal Code Lookup** and the request goes to `POST https://api.nextbillion.io/postalcode?key=…` instead of `/orbis/geocode/structured` (`nbPostalCode` in `nb.ts`; note `country` is required by the endpoint alongside `postalcode`).
- The response's `geopoint` renders as a result marker (row in the table, type `postalCode`) and the `boundary.multiPolygon` is converted to a GeoJSON MultiPolygon and drawn on the map — blue outline with translucent fill, inserted beneath the markers — with the view fitting the boundary.
- `ResultsMap` gained a `boundary` prop and a `viewRef` handle exposing the live map center.

**The deviation — `at` is NOT sent, and here's why**: you asked for `at` = centroid of the displayed view in the request body, and I built that (the `viewRef` plumbing is in place). But testing showed the Postcode API **ignores `postalcode` whenever `at` is present**: `{"postalcode":"43017","country":"USA","at":{lat LA}}` returns **91789 Walnut, CA** — the postal area at the map center — not 43017. In the demo (map defaults to LA) every lookup would return the map's own zip regardless of what was typed. Without `at`, 43017 correctly returns Dublin, OH with its boundary (browser-verified). So the request omits `at`; the code comments document the finding. If you'd rather have the "what zip is the map looking at" behavior (sending `at` and ignoring the typed code), it's a two-line flip — say the word.

Ready to build/deploy/commit/push.

# ---- nb.ts ----
p='src/lib/nb.ts'; s=open(p).read()
old='''// Fetch the full record for a previously returned result id.'''
new='''// Batch Routing API: submit up to 20 routing queries in one POST /batch call
// (each requests[].query is a full path string, e.g. "/directions/json?…"),
// then poll GET /batch?track_id=… until the batch resolves. There is no
// /orbis variant of this endpoint. Note: although the docs say only Isochrone
// queries are accepted, Directions queries work (verified live).
export interface BatchRouteResult {
  statusCode: number;
  distanceM: number | null;
  durationSec: number | null;
}

export async function nbBatchDirections(
  pairs: { origin: string; destination: string }[], // "lat,lng" strings
  apiKey: string,
  mode = "car"
): Promise<BatchRouteResult[]> {
  const submit = await fetch(
    `https://api.nextbillion.io/batch?key=${encodeURIComponent(apiKey)}`,
    {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
      body: JSON.stringify({
        requests: pairs.map((p) => ({
          query: `/directions/json?origin=${p.origin}&destination=${p.destination}&mode=${mode}&key=${apiKey}`,
        })),
      }),
    }
  );
  const created = await submit.json();
  if (!submit.ok || !created.track_id) {
    throw new Error(`Batch submit failed: ${created.msg ?? submit.status}`);
  }
  // Poll for the result (batches usually resolve in a few seconds).
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 30; attempt++) {
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 2000));
    const poll = await fetch(
      `https://api.nextbillion.io/batch?track_id=${created.track_id}&key=${encodeURIComponent(apiKey)}`
    );
    const data = await poll.json();
    if (data.status === "pending") continue;
    if (data.status !== "success") {
      throw new Error(`Batch failed: ${data.msg ?? data.status}`);
    }
    type Resp = {
      status_code: number;
      response?: { routes?: { distance?: number; duration?: number }[] };
    };
    return ((data.responses ?? []) as Resp[]).map((r) => {
      const route = r.response?.routes?.[0];
      return {
        statusCode: r.status_code,
        distanceM: route?.distance ?? null,
        durationSec: route?.duration ?? null,
      };
    });
  }
  throw new Error("Batch timed out (still pending after 60s)");
}

// Fetch the full record for a previously returned result id.'''

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Example 7 — Batch Routing (random directions queries in one batch)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

const ROUTING_BATCH_MAX = 20; // Batch Routing API limit per batch

// Random point within ~8km of a city centre, as a "lat,lng" string.
function randomPointNear(at: string): string {
  const [lat, lng] = at.split(",").map(Number);
  const dLat = (Math.random() - 0.5) * 0.15;
  const dLng = (Math.random() - 0.5) * 0.15;
  return `${(lat + dLat).toFixed(5)},${(lng + dLng).toFixed(5)}`;
}

function fmtKm(m: number | null): string {
  return m == null ? "" : `${(m / 1000).toFixed(1)} km`;
}

function fmtMin(sec: number | null): string {
  if (sec == null) return "";
  const min = sec / 60;
  return min >= 60
    ? `${Math.floor(min / 60)} h ${Math.round(min % 60)} min`
    : `${Math.round(min)} min`;
}

export function BatchRoutingExample({ apiKey }: ExampleProps) {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(5);
  const [rows, setRows] = useState<
    {
      origin: string;
      destination: string;
      city: string;
      result: { statusCode: number; distanceM: number | null; durationSec: number | null } | null;
    }[]
  >([]);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);
  const [elapsedMs, setElapsedMs] = useState<number | null>(null);
  const [error, setError] = useState("");

  async function run() {
    if (loading) return;
    const n = Math.min(Math.max(1, Math.floor(count) || 1), ROUTING_BATCH_MAX);
    setCount(n);
    setLoading(true);
    setError("");
    setElapsedMs(null);
    // Random origin/destination pairs, each within one metro area so the
    // routes are drivable.
    const pairs = Array.from({ length: n }, () => {
      const c = BATCH_CITIES[Math.floor(Math.random() * BATCH_CITIES.length)];
      return {
        city: `${c.city}, ${c.state}`,
        origin: randomPointNear(c.at),
        destination: randomPointNear(c.at),
      };
    });
    const started = performance.now();
    try {
      const results = await nbBatchDirections(
        pairs.map((p) => ({ origin: p.origin, destination: p.destination })),
        apiKey
      );
      setElapsedMs(performance.now() - started);
      setRows(pairs.map((p, i) => ({ ...p, result: results[i] ?? null })));
    } catch (e) {
      setError(String((e as Error)?.message ?? e));
      setRows([]);
    } finally {
      setLoading(false);
    }
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-end gap-3">
        <label className="flex flex-col gap-1 text-[9pt] text-gray-600">
          <span>Number of random routes (1–{ROUTING_BATCH_MAX})</span>
          <input
            type="number"
            min={1}
            max={ROUTING_BATCH_MAX}
            className="w-40 rounded border border-gray-300 px-2 py-1 text-sm"
            value={count}
            onChange={(e) => setCount(Number(e.target.value))}
            onKeyDown={(e) => {
              if (e.key === "Enter") run();
            }}
          />
        </label>
        <button
          type="button"
          className="rounded bg-blue-600 px-4 py-1.5 text-sm font-medium text-white disabled:opacity-50"
          disabled={loading}
          onClick={run}
        >
          {loading ? "Routing…" : "Batch Route"}
        </button>
        {elapsedMs != null && (
          <span className="pb-1.5 text-[9pt] text-gray-500">
            {rows.length} routes in {(elapsedMs / 1000).toFixed(2)}s
          </span>
        )}
      </div>
      {error && <div className="text-sm text-red-600">{error}</div>}
      {rows.length > 0 && (
        <div className="max-h-96 overflow-auto rounded border border-gray-300 bg-white">
          <table className="data-table">
            <thead>
              <tr>
                <th>#</th>
                <th>Area</th>
                <th>Origin</th>
                <th>Destination</th>
                <th>Travel Time</th>
                <th>Distance</th>
              </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody>
              {rows.map((row, i) => (
                <tr key={i}>
                  <td>{i + 1}</td>
                  <td>{row.city}</td>
                  <td>{row.origin}</td>
                  <td>{row.destination}</td>
                  <td>
                    {row.result?.statusCode === 200 ? (
                      fmtMin(row.result.durationSec)
                    ) : (
                      <i>no route ({row.result?.statusCode ?? "—"})</i>
                    )}
                  </td>
                  <td>{row.result?.statusCode === 200 ? fmtKm(row.result.distanceM) : ""}</td>
                </tr>
              ))}
            </tbody>
          </table>
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}'''

### CLAUDE (2026-08-25T13:53:18.106Z)

Both parts done:

**Answer to your question: no — there is no orbis variant of `/batch`.** `POST /orbis/batch` returns 404 (as does `/h/batch`); only `POST https://api.nextbillion.io/batch` exists. One useful find beyond the docs you pasted: although they say the batch accepts *only Isochrone* queries, **Directions queries work** (verified live: `/directions/json?…` inside a batch returns 200 with distance/duration) — which is what makes the new example possible. Geocode/search queries do *not* work inside it (404 per-request).

**Example 7 — Batch Routing** (local only):
- "Number of random routes (1–20)" input (20 = the API's per-batch limit) + **Batch Route** button.
- Generates N random origin/destination pairs, each within ~8 km of one metro center (LA, Columbus, Las Vegas, NY, Seattle, Boston) so routes are drivable, submits them as one `POST /batch` with `requests[].query = "/directions/json?…"`, then polls `GET /batch?track_id=…` every 2 s (60 s timeout).
- Result table: **# / Area / Origin / Destination / Travel Time / Distance** (h/min + km; failed queries show "no route (code)"), plus a "N routes in X.XXs" note.
- `nbBatchDirections()` in `nb.ts` documents the no-orbis-variant finding and the docs discrepancy.

Browser-verified: 8 routes in 6.98 s, all rows populated (e.g. LA 34.07281,-118.30695 → 34.12195,-118.17860: 20 min, 16.6 km).

Ready to build/deploy/commit/push on your word.

### CLAUDE (2026-08-25T14:04:21.455Z)

[tool: Bash — Replace GeoJSON namespace with local BoundaryFeature type]
```bash
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='src/lib/nb.ts'; s=open(p).read()
old='''export interface PostalCodeResult {
  feature: SearchFeature;
  boundary: GeoJSON.Feature | null;
}'''
new='''// Minimal GeoJSON feature type for the boundary polygons (avoids depending
// on the ambient GeoJSON namespace from @types/geojson).
export interface BoundaryFeature {
  type: "Feature";
  properties: Record<string, unknown>;
  geometry: { type: "MultiPolygon"; coordinates: number[][][][] };
}

export interface PostalCodeResult {
  feature: SearchFeature;
  boundary: BoundaryFeature | null;
}'''
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new)
s=s.replace('    const boundary: GeoJSON.Feature | null = coords.length','    const boundary: BoundaryFeature | null = coords.length')
open(p,'w').write(s)

p='src/components/Examples.tsx'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('import type { BatchGeocodeQuery, StructuredQuery } from "@/lib/nb";','import type { BatchGeocodeQuery, BoundaryFeature, StructuredQuery } from "@/lib/nb";')
s=s.replace('  const [boundary, setBoundary] = useState<GeoJSON.Feature | null>(null);','  const [boundary, setBoundary] = useState<BoundaryFeature | null>(null);')
open(p,'w').write(s)

p='src/components/ResultsMap.tsx'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
import type { SearchFeature } from "@/lib/types";''','''import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
import type { BoundaryFeature } from "@/lib/nb";
import type { SearchFeature } from "@/lib/types";''')
s=s.replace('  boundary?: GeoJSON.Feature | null;','  boundary?: BoundaryFeature | null;')
# boundary.geometry?.type check stays valid
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
grep -rn "GeoJSON\." src; npx tsc --noEmit -p . && npm run build 2>&1 | grep -E "error|✓ Compiled"
```

### CLAUDE (2026-08-26T12:00:39.206Z)

[tool: Bash — Rewrite BatchRoutingExample with parallel batches; build]
```bash
python3 - <<'PYEOF'
p='src/components/Examples.tsx'; s=open(p).read()
start=s.index('const ROUTING_BATCH_MAX = 20; // Batch Routing API limit per batch')
new_block = '''const ROUTING_BATCH_MAX = 20; // Batch Routing API limit per batch
const ROUTING_BATCHES_MAX = 10; // how many batches may run in parallel

// Random point within ~8km of a city centre, as a "lat,lng" string.
function randomPointNear(at: string): string {
  const [lat, lng] = at.split(",").map(Number);
  const dLat = (Math.random() - 0.5) * 0.15;
  const dLng = (Math.random() - 0.5) * 0.15;
  return `${(lat + dLat).toFixed(5)},${(lng + dLng).toFixed(5)}`;
}

function fmtKm(m: number | null): string {
  return m == null ? "" : `${(m / 1000).toFixed(1)} km`;
}

function fmtMin(sec: number | null): string {
  if (sec == null) return "";
  const min = sec / 60;
  return min >= 60
    ? `${Math.floor(min / 60)} h ${Math.round(min % 60)} min`
    : `${Math.round(min)} min`;
}

interface RouteRow {
  batch: number; // 1-based batch number
  city: string;
  origin: string;
  destination: string;
  status: "pending" | "done" | "error";
  result: { statusCode: number; distanceM: number | null; durationSec: number | null } | null;
  error?: string;
}

export function BatchRoutingExample({ apiKey }: ExampleProps) {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(5);
  const [batches, setBatches] = useState(1);
  const [rows, setRows] = useState<RouteRow[]>([]);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);
  const [doneBatches, setDoneBatches] = useState(0);
  const [totalBatches, setTotalBatches] = useState(0);
  const [elapsedMs, setElapsedMs] = useState<number | null>(null);
  const [error, setError] = useState("");

  async function run() {
    if (loading) return;
    const perBatch = Math.min(Math.max(1, Math.floor(count) || 1), ROUTING_BATCH_MAX);
    const batchCount = Math.min(
      Math.max(1, Math.floor(batches) || 1),
      ROUTING_BATCHES_MAX
    );
    setCount(perBatch);
    setBatches(batchCount);
    setLoading(true);
    setError("");
    setElapsedMs(null);
    setDoneBatches(0);
    setTotalBatches(batchCount);

    // Random origin/destination pairs, each within one metro area so the
    // routes are drivable. Every query is listed up front as "pending" so the
    // table fills in progressively as each batch resolves.
    const plan: RouteRow[][] = Array.from({ length: batchCount }, (_, b) =>
      Array.from({ length: perBatch }, () => {
        const c = BATCH_CITIES[Math.floor(Math.random() * BATCH_CITIES.length)];
        return {
          batch: b + 1,
          city: `${c.city}, ${c.state}`,
          origin: randomPointNear(c.at),
          destination: randomPointNear(c.at),
          status: "pending" as const,
          result: null,
        };
      })
    );
    setRows(plan.flat());

    const started = performance.now();
    // All batches are submitted at once and polled independently; each one
    // writes its own rows the moment it comes back.
    await Promise.all(
      plan.map(async (batchRows, b) => {
        try {
          const results = await nbBatchDirections(
            batchRows.map((r) => ({ origin: r.origin, destination: r.destination })),
            apiKey
          );
          setRows((prev) =>
            prev.map((row) => {
              if (row.batch !== b + 1) return row;
              const idx = batchRows.findIndex((r) => r === row || r.origin === row.origin);
              return {
                ...row,
                status: "done" as const,
                result: results[idx] ?? null,
              };
            })
          );
        } catch (e) {
          const msg = String((e as Error)?.message ?? e);
          setRows((prev) =>
            prev.map((row) =>
              row.batch === b + 1 ? { ...row, status: "error" as const, error: msg } : row
            )
          );
          setError((prev) => prev || `Batch ${b + 1}: ${msg}`);
        } finally {
          setDoneBatches((n) => n + 1);
        }
      })
    );
    setElapsedMs(performance.now() - started);
    setLoading(false);
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-end gap-3">
        <label className="flex flex-col gap-1 text-[9pt] text-gray-600">
          <span>Routes per batch (1–{ROUTING_BATCH_MAX})</span>
          <input
            type="number"
            min={1}
            max={ROUTING_BATCH_MAX}
            className="w-40 rounded border border-gray-300 px-2 py-1 text-sm"
            value={count}
            onChange={(e) => setCount(Number(e.target.value))}
            onKeyDown={(e) => {
              if (e.key === "Enter") run();
            }}
          />
        </label>
        <label className="flex flex-col gap-1 text-[9pt] text-gray-600">
          <span>Number of batches (1–{ROUTING_BATCHES_MAX})</span>
          <input
            type="number"
            min={1}
            max={ROUTING_BATCHES_MAX}
            className="w-40 rounded border border-gray-300 px-2 py-1 text-sm"
            value={batches}
            onChange={(e) => setBatches(Number(e.target.value))}
            onKeyDown={(e) => {
              if (e.key === "Enter") run();
            }}
          />
        </label>
        <button
          type="button"
          className="rounded bg-blue-600 px-4 py-1.5 text-sm font-medium text-white disabled:opacity-50"
          disabled={loading}
          onClick={run}
        >
          {loading ? "Routing…" : "Batch Route"}
        </button>
        {totalBatches > 0 && (
          <span className="pb-1.5 text-[9pt] text-gray-500">
            {loading
              ? `${doneBatches} / ${totalBatches} batches complete…`
              : `${rows.length} routes in ${totalBatches} batch${totalBatches > 1 ? "es" : ""}` +
                (elapsedMs != null ? ` in ${(elapsedMs / 1000).toFixed(2)}s` : "")}
          </span>
        )}
      </div>
      {error && <div className="text-sm text-red-600">{error}</div>}
      {rows.length > 0 && (
        <div className="max-h-96 overflow-auto rounded border border-gray-300 bg-white">
          <table className="data-table">
            <thead>
              <tr>
                <th>#</th>
                <th>Batch</th>
                <th>Area</th>
                <th>Origin</th>
                <th>Destination</th>
                <th>Travel Time</th>
                <th>Distance</th>
              </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody>
              {rows.map((row, i) => (
                <tr key={i}>
                  <td>{i + 1}</td>
                  <td>{row.batch}</td>
                  <td>{row.city}</td>
                  <td>{row.origin}</td>
                  <td>{row.destination}</td>
                  <td>
                    {row.status === "pending" ? (
                      <span className="text-gray-400">waiting…</span>
                    ) : row.status === "error" ? (
                      <i className="text-red-600">failed</i>
                    ) : row.result?.statusCode === 200 ? (
                      fmtMin(row.result.durationSec)
                    ) : (
                      <i>no route ({row.result?.statusCode ?? "—"})</i>
                    )}
                  </td>
                  <td>
                    {row.status === "done" && row.result?.statusCode === 200
                      ? fmtKm(row.result.distanceM)
                      : ""}
                  </td>
                </tr>
              ))}
            </tbody>
          </table>
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
'''
s = s[:start] + new_block
open(p,'w').write(s)
PYEOF
npx tsc --noEmit -p . && npm run build 2>&1 | grep -E "error|✓ Compiled"
```

  const [error, setError] = useState("");

    if (loading) return;

    const batchCount = Math.min(
      Math.max(1, Math.floor(batches) || 1),
      BATCH_GEOCODE_BATCHES_MAX
    );
    setCount(perBatch);
    setBatches(batchCount);
    setLoading(true);
    setError("");
    setElapsedMs(null);
    setDoneBatches(0);
    setTotalBatches(batchCount);

    // Every generated address is listed up front as "pending" so the table
    // fills in progressively as each batch resolves.
    const plan: BatchGeocodeQuery[][] = Array.from({ length: batchCount }, () =>
      randomBatchQueries(perBatch)
    );
    setRows(
      plan.flatMap((queries, b) =>
        queries.map((q, i) => ({
          batch: b + 1,
          indexInBatch: i,
          query: q.q,
          status: "pending" as const,
          result: null,
        }))
      )
    );

    const started = performance.now();
    // All batches are submitted at once; each one writes its own rows the
    // moment it comes back.
    await Promise.all(

          const results = await nbBatchGeocode(queries, apiKey);
          setRows((prev) =>
            prev.map((row) =>
              row.batch === b + 1
                ? {
                    ...row,
                    status: "done" as const,
                    result: results[row.indexInBatch]?.[0] ?? null,
                  }
                : row
            )
          );

          setRows((prev) =>
            prev.map((row) =>
              row.batch === b + 1 ? { ...row, status: "error" as const } : row
            )
          );
          setError((prev) => prev || `Batch ${b + 1}: ${msg}`);
        } finally {
          setDoneBatches((n) => n + 1);
        }
      })
    );

    setLoading(false);
  }

        <label className="flex flex-col gap-1 text-[9pt] text-gray-600">
          <span>Addresses per batch (1–{BATCH_MAX})</span>
          <input
            type="number"
            min={1}
            max={BATCH_MAX}
            className="w-40 rounded border border-gray-300 px-2 py-1 text-sm"
            value={count}
            onChange={(e) => setCount(Number(e.target.value))}
            onKeyDown={(e) => {
              if (e.key === "Enter") run();
            }}
          />
        </label>
        <label className="flex flex-col gap-1 text-[9pt] text-gray-600">
          <span>Number of batches (1–{BATCH_GEOCODE_BATCHES_MAX})</span>
          <input

            min={1}

            value={batches}
            onChange={(e) => setBatches(Number(e.target.value))}
            onKeyDown={(e) => {
              if (e.key === "Enter") run();
            }}
          />
        </label>
        <button
          type="button"
          className="rounded bg-blue-600 px-4 py-1.5 text-sm font-medium text-white disabled:opacity-50"
          disabled={loading}
          onClick={run}
        >
          {loading ? "Geocoding…" : "Batch Geocode"}
        </button>
        {totalBatches > 0 && (
          <span className="pb-1.5 text-[9pt] text-gray-500">
            {loading
              ? `${doneBatches} / ${totalBatches} batches complete…`
              : `${rows.length} queries in ${totalBatches} batch${totalBatches > 1 ? "es" : ""}` +
                (elapsedMs != null ? ` in ${(elapsedMs / 1000).toFixed(2)}s` : "")}
          </span>
        )}
      </div>
      {error && <div className="text-sm text-red-600">{error}</div>}
      {rows.length > 0 && (
        <div className="max-h-96 overflow-auto rounded border border-gray-300 bg-white">
          <table className="data-table">
            <thead>
              <tr>
                <th>#</th>
                <th>Batch</th>
                <th>Generated Address</th>
                <th>Result</th>
                <th>Type</th>
                <th>Scoring</th>
                <th>Position</th>
              </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody>
              {rows.map((row, i) => (
                <tr key={i}>

                  <td>{row.batch}</td>
                  <td className="max-w-[280px]">{row.query}</td>
                  <td className="max-w-[360px]">
                    {row.status === "pending" ? (
                      <span className="text-gray-400">waiting…</span>
                    ) : row.status === "error" ? (
                      <i className="text-red-600">failed</i>

                  </td>
                  <td>{row.result?.resultType ?? ""}</td>
                  <td>

                  </td>
                  <td>{fmtLatLng(row.result?.center)}</td>
                </tr>
              ))}
            </tbody>
          </table>
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Deploy runbook** (Cloud Build denied): local `docker build --platform=linux/amd64 --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_NB_API_KEY=…` → `docker push` → `cd terraform && terraform apply -auto-approve -var image=$IMG` (ALWAYS pass `-var image` or the service resets to the placeholder image). Tag format `YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS` UTC. `gcloud auth login` token expires frequently — the user must run `! gcloud auth login`. Docker Desktop may need `open -a Docker`.
   - **Orbis vs legacy `/h` API differences** (all verified live): `lang` must be BCP-47 region-qualified (`en-US`, `fr-FR`; bare `ar` works; ja/eo/my/yo/zh-Hans rejected); no `/orbis/autosuggest` (404); ids are not interchangeable between bases; score is top-level `score` (not `scoring.queryScore`) and not 0–1 scale; `address.label` is address-only (POI name only in `title`); no `type` field; no `highlights`.
   - **No orbis variants**: `/orbis/geocode/batch` → 404 (only `/geocode/batch`); `/orbis/batch` → 404 (only `/batch`); `/orbis/postalcode` not used (only `/postalcode`).
   - **Batch Routing API** (`POST /batch`): body `{requests:[{query:"/directions/json?…&key=…"}]}`, returns `track_id`; poll `GET /batch?track_id=…&key=…` until `status !== "pending"`; max 20 queries/batch. Docs say isochrone-only but **Directions queries work** (verified).
   - **Postcode API** (`POST /postalcode`): body `{postalcode, country, at?}`; `country` required with `postalcode`; **`at` overrides `postalcode`** (verified: 43017 + LA `at` → 91789 Walnut CA); response `places[].boundary.multiPolygon[].polygon[].points[{lat,lng}]`.
   - **MapLibre/NB maps SDK**: `map.setStyle()` wipes custom sources/layers → re-apply on `style.load`; `setLayerZoomRange` for POI clamping; `fill-color`/`fill-outline-color` zoom interpolation for footprint emphasis; DOM click handler registered once on the map survives style swaps (uses a ref to the latest callback).
   - **Browser testing quirk**: an occluded/background Chrome tab suspends rAF so the map never renders — fixed with AppleScript that activates the tab. Also, the first click after `scroll_to`/`form_input` often doesn't register; clicking again by ref works.
   - **Parallel batch pattern**: pre-render all rows with `status: "pending"`, fire `Promise.all` over batches, each batch updates only its own rows matched by an explicit `indexInBatch` (never by object reference).

     - `itemToFeature` handles both score shapes and composes placeName:
       ```ts
       // /orbis returns a top-level `score`; the legacy /h shape was scoring.queryScore.
       scoring: typeof itm.score === "number" ? itm.score : itm.scoring?.queryScore,
       // /h labels embedded the POI name ("Starbucks, 505 N Grand Ave…"); /orbis
       // labels are address-only, so prepend the title when it isn't already there.
       const placeName = isQuery ? title
         : label && title && !label.toLowerCase().includes(title.toLowerCase())
           ? `${title}, ${label}` : label || title;
       ```
     - `nbGeocode` minimal shape: `${NB_H}/geocode?in=countryCode:${countryList(panel)}&q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}&at=${panel.city.centroid}&key=…`

         // present (verified live: 43017 + an LA `at` returns 91789), so the
         // map-view centroid must NOT be sent here or the entered postal code
         // would never be looked up.
         const places = await nbPostalCode(
           { postalcode: query.postalCode!.trim(), country: query.countryCode.trim() }, apiKey);
         setFeatures(places.map((p) => p.feature));
         setBoundary(places[0]?.boundary ?? null);
       }
       ```

       ```ts
       await Promise.all(plan.map(async (queries, b) => {
         try {
           const results = await nbBatchGeocode(queries, apiKey);
           setRows(prev => prev.map(row => row.batch === b + 1
             ? { ...row, status: "done" as const, result: results[row.indexInBatch]?.[0] ?? null }
             : row));
         } catch (e) { /* mark that batch's rows "error", setError once */ }
         finally { setDoneBatches(n => n + 1); }
       }));
       ```

];

function pickPosType() {

}

```

- **Frequency** is now a random pick from `[0.25, 0.5, 1, 2]`, uniform. Over a 40-row sample: 7 / 12 / 11 / 10. This replaced the RRULE-based cadence generator entirely — `randomVisitPlan`, `FEMSA_BLOCKS` and `FEMSA_SINGLE_DAYS` are gone, since nothing consumed the day sets or RRULE strings any more.
- **Service Time** in minutes (`MIN_SERVICE_MIN = 7` / `MAX_SERVICE_MIN = 50`); sample range 9–50.
- **Available / Unavailable Days** as before — random Mon–Fri letter subset, at most one restricted day drawn from the days not already available.

**One thing to be aware of with the `M,T,W,T,F` format:** because Tuesday and Thursday share the letter `T`, rows like `avail="T,F" unavail="T"` show up. That's not a bug — internally the days are indices, so that row means available Tue+Fri, restricted Thu — but a consumer parsing the letters alone can't tell the two `T`s apart, and ~25% of rows land in that state. If whatever reads this CSV matches on letters, tell me and I'll switch to `MO,TU,WE,TH,FR` or emit a fixed 5-slot mask like `M,-,W,-,F`.

I also have to flag a self-inflicted problem from this turn: my dead-code removal cut too wide again and deleted `randCoord` plus the whole US mock-data block.
